  • Ek hi chhote office pe ek saath das stringers mat bhejo — bahar nikaal denge (politeness).
  • Important boards (shehar ka centre) door ke gaon se zyada baar dekho (priority, freshness).
  • Jo notice pehle se hai uski dobara photo mat lo (content dedup), aur jo address pehle se list mein hai wahan dobara mat jao (URL dedup).
  • Kuch buildings pe likha hai "peeche waale kamre mein photo mana hai" (robots.txt).
  • Us building se bacho jiski seedhiyan kabhi khatam nahi hoti (spider trap).

docs.title: Step 1 · Scope
docs.text:
Crawler kis liye hai? Isse design badalta hai:

Purpose Example Zor kis pe Search engine indexing Googlebot, Bingbot Scale, freshness, priority Web archiving Internet Archive, national libraries Completeness, long-term storage Web mining / data collection Market research, training datasets Targeted domains, extraction Web monitoring Brand/copyright/price monitoring Specific sites, recrawl frequency

Clarifying baatcheet

Tum: Crawl kis liye hai? — Interviewer: Search engine index ke liye. Tum: Kitne pages, kitni baar? — I: Mahine mein lagbhag 2 billion pages. Tum: Content types? — I: Abhi sirf HTML. Tum: Naye/edit hue pages bhi? — I: Haan, freshness matter karti hai. Tum: Pages store karne hain? Kitne time? — I: Raw HTML 3 saal. Tum: Duplicate pages? — I: Duplicate content skip karo.

Achhe crawler ki khoobiyan:

  • Scalability — billions of pages → massively parallel.
  • Robustness — web toote HTML, jawab na dene waale servers, crashes, malicious links se bhara hai. Girna nahi hai.
  • Politeness — kisi site pe thode time mein bahut requests mat thoko.
  • Extensibility — naya content type (images, PDFs) jodna plug-in hona chahiye, redesign nahi.

docs.title: Estimates
docs.text: Cheez Value Pages/mahina 2 B Average download rate 2 B / (30 × 86,400) ≈ 770 pages/s Peak (×2) ~1,500 pages/s Average page size ~300 KB Storage/mahina 2 B × 300 KB = 600 TB 3 saal ka storage 600 TB × 36 ≈ 21.6 PB (compress karo! HTML 5–10× compress hota hai) Download bandwidth 1,500 × 300 KB ≈ 450 MB/s ≈ peak pe 3.6 Gbps

docs.title: Step 2 · High-level design
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    SEED[Seed URLs] --> FR[[URL Frontier]]
    FR --> DL[HTML Downloader]
    DNS[(DNS resolver<br/>+ cache)] --- DL
    ROB[(robots.txt cache)] --- DL
    DL --> PAR[Content parser]
    PAR --> CS{Content seen?}
    CS -->|duplicate| X1[discard]
    CS -->|naya| ST[(Content storage)]
    CS -->|naya| LE[Link extractor]
    LE --> UF[URL filter]
    UF --> US{URL seen?}
    US -->|dekha hua| X2[discard]
    US -->|naya| UST[(URL storage)]
    US -->|naya| FR
Component Kaam Seed URLs Shuruaati points. Aise chuno ki web achhe se cover ho — jaise locality se (har desh ki popular sites) ya topic se (news, shopping, sports, education…). URL Frontier Download karne waali list (sabse simple mein FIFO — par practice mein kahin smarter, neeche dekho). HTML Downloader HTTP pe pages laata hai. DNS Resolver Hostnames ko IPs mein badalta hai (cached). Content Parser HTML parse aur validate karta hai; kharab pages drop. Alag component rakho taaki slow parsing downloads block na kare. Content Seen? Woh pages pakadta hai jinka content pehle se hai — web ka bada hissa duplicate hai (mirrors, syndication, printer-friendly copies). Poora text nahi, hashes compare karo. Content Storage Zyada tar content disk pe (blob storage, compressed); popular content memory mein cached. Link Extractor HTML se links nikaalta hai aur relative links ko absolute banata hai (/about → https://site.in/about). URL Filter Unwanted URLs hatata hai: kuch file types/extensions, error-prone links, blacklisted sites. URL Seen? Pehle visit ya queue hue URLs skip karta hai (loops aur repeat kaam se bachata hai). Bloom filter ya hash table. URL Storage Visit hue URLs ka record.

docs.title: Crawl loop, step by step
docs.text:
1. Seed URLs frontier mein daalo.
  2. Downloader frontier se URLs leta hai, DNS resolve karta hai, page download karta hai.
  3. Parser parse karke check karta hai ki valid hai.
  4. "Content seen?" — exact same content hai toh drop.
  5. Warna store karo aur link extractor ko bhejo.
  6. Nikle links URL filter se guzarte hain.
  7. "URL seen?" — naye URLs URL storage aur frontier mein; jaane-pehchaane drop.
  8. Repeat.

docs.title: BFS, DFS nahi
docs.text:
Web ek directed graph hai: pages nodes, links edges. DFS ek site mein bewajah gehraai tak ghus jaata hai aur kho sakta hai. BFS (FIFO queue) usual base hai. Par plain BFS ki do problems:

  1. Impoliteness. Page ke zyada tar links same host ki taraf jaate hain. wiki.example.org/... URLs se bhari FIFO queue matlab hamare saare parallel workers ek saath us ek host pe gir padte hain — practically DoS.
  2. Priority nahi. Random forum post aur badi news homepage ko barabar treatment. Hume important aur jaldi badalne waale pages pehle chahiye.

URL frontier dono fix karta hai.

docs.title: URL frontier
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    IN[Naye URLs] --> PZ[Prioritizer]
    PZ --> F1[["Front queue f1<br/>(sabse high priority)"]]
    PZ --> F2[["f2"]]
    PZ --> Fn[["fn (sabse low)"]]
    F1 & F2 & Fn --> QS["Front queue selector<br/>(random, high priority ki taraf jhuka)"]
    QS --> BR["Back queue router<br/>(host → queue table use karta hai)"]
    MT[("Mapping table<br/>host → back queue")] --- BR
    BR --> B1[["Back queue b1<br/>sirf news.example.in"]]
    BR --> B2[["b2<br/>sirf shop.example.com"]]
    BR --> Bn[["bn<br/>sirf some-blog.in"]]
    B1 --> W1[Worker 1]
    B2 --> W2[Worker 2]
    Bn --> Wn[Worker n]

Front queues → priority. Ek prioritizer har URL ko score deta hai — PageRank/link popularity, site traffic, update frequency, root se depth ke hisaab se — aur n front queues mein se ek mein daalta hai (f1 = sabse high). Queue selector front queues se random chunta hai par high priority ki taraf jhuka hua, taaki important pages pehle jaayein aur low-priority waale bhi aage badhte rahein.

Back queues → politeness. Har back queue mein sirf ek host ke URLs. Mapping table host → back queue record karti hai. Har back queue ko ek worker thread khaali karta hai, jo ek baar mein ek page download karta hai aur requests ke beech delay karta hai (jaise kuch seconds, ya robots.txt mein jo Crawl-delay likha ho). Toh kisi host ko hamari taraf se kabhi ek se zyada concurrent request nahi milti.

Mapping table news.example.in b1 shop.example.com b2 … … some-blog.in bn 
/** Minimal politeness scheduler: har host ki ek queue, same host ke fetches ke beech min delay. */
final class PoliteFrontier {
    private final Map<String, Deque<String>> perHost = new HashMap<>();
    private final PriorityQueue<Map.Entry<String, Long>> ready =      // host → sabse jaldi agla-fetch time
        new PriorityQueue<>(Map.Entry.comparingByValue());
    private final long delayMs;

    PoliteFrontier(long delayMs) { this.delayMs = delayMs; }

    synchronized void add(String url) {
        String host = java.net.URI.create(url).getHost();
        Deque<String> q = perHost.computeIfAbsent(host, h -> new ArrayDeque<>());
        if (q.isEmpty()) ready.add(Map.entry(host, System.currentTimeMillis()));
        q.addLast(url);
    }

    /** Agla URL jiske host ko abhi hit karna allowed hai, ya null. */
    synchronized String next() {
        Map.Entry<String, Long> head = ready.peek();
        if (head == null || head.getValue() > System.currentTimeMillis()) return null;
        ready.poll();
        Deque<String> q = perHost.get(head.getKey());
        String url = q.pollFirst();
        if (!q.isEmpty()) ready.add(Map.entry(head.getKey(), System.currentTimeMillis() + delayMs));
        return url;
    }
}

Freshness. Pages badalte hain; recrawl karna padta hai. Sab kuch recrawl karna barbaadi hai, toh:

  • Har page ki update history ke hisaab se recrawl (jo page pichli 3 visits mein badla, use jaldi dobara dekho).
  • Important pages zyada baar recrawl.
  • HTTP conditional requests (If-Modified-Since / ETag) use karo taaki unchanged pages ka kharcha bas ek chhota sa 304 Not Modified ho.

Frontier storage. Saikdon million URLs memory mein nahi aate, aur pure disk slow hai. Hybrid: frontier ka zyada hissa disk pe, enqueue/dequeue ke liye in-memory buffers jo batches mein flush/refill hote hain.

docs.title: HTML downloader
docs.text:
robots.txt (Robots Exclusion Protocol) crawlers ko batata hai kya fetch kar sakte hain. Crawl karne se pehle har host ka laao, cache karo (roz refresh), aur maano:

User-agent: *
Disallow: /cart/
Disallow: /search
Crawl-delay: 5

User-agent: MyCrawlerBot
Allow: /

Downloads tez banana. ~1,500 pages/s pe downloader zyada time wait karta hai, toh fayda waits hatane se aata hai:

Wait Fix DNS lookups (10–200 ms, aksar blocking) Background mein refresh hone waala local DNS cache; async resolver Slow ya mare hue servers Aggressive connect/read timeouts (kuch seconds) aur aage badho Lambe network paths Kai regions mein crawler fleets; har ek apne paas ke hosts crawl kare Har request pe ek thread Async HTTP clients jo kai hosts ke across hazaaron connections rakhein Ek machine ki capacity Kai crawler machines; URL space ko consistent hashing se host ke hisaab se baanto, taaki har host ka politeness state exactly ek machine pe rahe

Zinda rehna. Crashes, kharab HTML aur dushman pages maan ke chalo:

Failure Bachav Crawler machine mar gayi Uske hosts padosiyon pe re-hash; frontier aur seen-sets durable storage mein checkpoint, toh kaam resume hota hai, restart nahi Page parser ko crash kar deta hai Size aur time limits waale isolated worker mein parse; sab catch karo, log karo, skip karo Kachra data Store karne se pehle validate (content type, encoding, size)

docs.title: Extensibility
docs.text:
Downloader ke baad sab kuch "page fetched" event ke subscribers ka set samjho. Core loop (parse → dedupe → links nikaalo) ek subscriber hai; nayi capabilities aur subscribers ki tarah judti hain, core ko chhue bina. Jaise ek PDF text extractor jo documents index kare, ya ek structured-data extractor jo schema.org markup se product prices aur ratings nikaale:

flowchart LR
    DL[Downloader] --> EV[["page-fetched events"]]
    EV --> CORE["Core: parse → dedupe → links nikaalo"]
    EV --> PDF["PDF text extractor<br/>(plug-in)"]
    EV --> SD["schema.org product extractor<br/>(plug-in)"]

docs.title: Dedup detail mein
docs.text:
Content seen? Har page body ko hash karo (jaise 64-bit fingerprint) aur set mein dekho. Exact hashes exact duplicates pakadte hain. Near-duplicates (same article, alag ads/timestamps) ke liye SimHash ya MinHash: milte-julte documents ke fingerprints kuch hi bits mein alag hote hain, toh chhoti Hamming distance waale pages flag karo.

URL seen? Pehle URLs normalise karo (host lower-case, default ports hatao, query params sort karo, fragments #… aur utm_* jaise tracking params hatao). Phir Bloom filter check karo: 10 billion URLs × ~10 bits ≈ 12.5 GB memory, 1% false positives (matlab kabhi-kabhi aisa URL skip ho jaayega jo asal mein nahi dekha — crawler ke liye chalega).

docs.title: Problematic content
docs.text:
• Redundant content — content dedup sambhalta hai.
  • Spider traps — pages jo infinite URLs banate hain, jaise calendar links (/calendar?month=… hamesha) ya site.in/a/b/c/a/b/c/…. Bachav: max URL length, har host pe max depth, har crawl mein har host ke max pages, repeat hote path patterns detect karna, aur jaane-maane traps ke liye manual blacklists.
  • Data noise — ads, code snippets, spam pages; jahan ho sake filter karo.

docs.title: Step 4 · Wrap-up — aur kya
docs.text:
Time bache toh yeh dhaage kheencho:

  • JavaScript-heavy sites. Kai pages apne links aur content browser mein banate hain. Headless-browser renderers ka pool sambhal sakta hai, par rendering plain fetch se 10–100× mehenga — sirf zaroori sites route karo.
  • Quantity se zyada quality. Filter stage pe spam/low-quality classifier storage, bandwidth aur index noise bachata hai.
  • Stores scale karna. URL store aur content store ko kisi bhi bade dataset ki tarah sharding (host ya URL hash se) aur replication chahiye (Chapters 1 aur 6).
  • Operations. Pages/s, har host ka error rate, robots.txt denials, frontier size aur freshness lag ke dashboards; alerts jab ek host ka URL count phoot jaaye (trap) ya download rate gire.
  • Achha naagrik banna. Bot ko saaf User-Agent aur contact URL ke saath identify karo, 429/503 pe peeche hato, aur site owners ki requests maano.

docs.title: Interviewer follow-ups
docs.text:
Kaise ensure karoge ki do crawler machines ek saath same host ko hit na karein?

URL nahi, host se partition karo: hash(host) → crawler machine (consistent hashing taaki machines join/leave kar sakein). Phir host ke saare URLs ek machine pe girte hain, jo har host ki ek back queue rakhti hai aur delay locally enforce karti hai — machines ke beech koi coordination nahi chahiye.

Tumhara crawler 1,000 pages/s download kar raha hai par CPU idle hai. Bottleneck kahan hai?

Shayad I/O waits: DNS lookups (cache nahi, ya synchronous resolver), bina timeouts ke slow servers, ya bahut kam concurrent connections. Fixes: DNS cache + async resolver, aggressive timeouts, async/non-blocking HTTP clients jo kai hosts ke across hazaaron concurrent connections rakhein, aur check karo ki politeness queues workers ko bhookha to nahi rakh rahi (frontier mein bahut kam alag hosts).

Kaunse URLs pehle crawl karne hain, yeh kaise prioritise karoge?

Score = f(page importance, change rate, staleness). Importance link-based rank (PageRank), domain authority aur traffic se; change rate pichli crawl history se; staleness = aakhri crawl se beeta time. Score ko front queues pe map karo aur selector ko high-priority queues ki taraf jhukao.

Unchanged pages dobara download karne se kaise bachoge?

If-Modified-Since / If-None-Match (ETag) ke saath conditional GETs → server bina body ke 304 Not Modified deta hai. Jo servers yeh support nahi karte, unke liye download ke baad content fingerprint compare karo aur reprocessing skip karo.

Aisa 'spider trap' jo kabhi pehle nahi dekha, use kaise handle karoge?

Generic limits zyada tar pakad lete hain: URL length cap, har host pe depth cap, har crawl cycle mein har host ka page budget, aur repeat hote path segments ya sirf counter badalne waale query parameters ka detection. Jab ek host ka discovered-URL count uske PageRank ke muqable phoot jaaye toh alert karo — phir insaan pattern blacklist kar sakta hai.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — Politeness throughput

Tumhara politeness rule hai "har host pe har 2 second mein ek request". 1,500 pages/s sustain karne ke liye frontier mein kisi bhi pal kam se kam kitne alag hosts active hone chahiye?

Solution. Har host max 0.5 pages/s deta hai → ≥ 1,500 / 0.5 = 3,000 active hosts chahiye (practice mein zyada, kyunki downloads mein time lagta hai aur kuch hosts slow hain). Isliye frontier ko sirf zyada URLs nahi, zyada hosts "garam" rakhne chahiye.

Practice 2 — Bloom filter memory

5 billion unique URLs expected hain aur 1% false positives chalenge. Bloom filter ki memory?

Solution. ~9.6 bits per element → 5 × 10⁹ × 9.6 ≈ 4.8 × 10¹⁰ bits ≈ 6 GB. Ek machine ki RAM mein, ya frontier ke saath host se shard karo.

Practice 3 — Focused crawler design karo

Ek crawler design karo jo 50,000 e-commerce product pages ko har ghante price changes ke liye dekhe. Search crawler se kya alag hai?

Solution. Discovery nahi (fixed URL list) → na link extraction, na URL-seen set. Frontier = agle due time se keyed scheduler. Politeness ab bhi zaroori (host se group, robots aur rate limits maano). Conditional GETs, sirf price nikaalo (har site ka selector, ya JS-heavy pages ke liye headless rendering), time series store karo, changes pe alert. 50K/ghanta ≈ 14 req/s — bahut chhota.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• Crawler use cases aur chaar properties bata sakta hoon: scalable, robust, polite, extensible.
  • Crawl ke liye QPS, storage aur bandwidth estimate kar sakta hoon.
  • Pipeline bana ke har component samjha sakta hoon.
  • Samjha sakta hoon ki plain BFS impolite aur unprioritised kyun hai, aur front/back queues kaise fix karti hain.
  • robots.txt, DNS caching, locality, timeouts, aur host se partitioning pata hai.
  • Content dedup (hash, SimHash) aur URL dedup (normalisation + Bloom filter) samjha sakta hoon.
  • Spider-trap bachav aur freshness strategies bata sakta hoon.

Aage: 10 · Notification System

docs.title: 10 · Notification System Design karo
docs.text:
⏱ 40 min read 🔥 Classic "async pipeline" design Book: Chapter 10

TL;DR

  • Notifications third-party providers se jaati hain: APNs (iOS push), FCM (Android/web push), SMS gateways (Twilio, MSG91…), email services (SES, SendGrid…). Devices tak hum khud deliver nahi karte.
  • Services ek notification service (API) ko call karti hain jo validate karti hai, user preferences aur rate limits check karti hai, template render karti hai, aur job ko har channel ki queue mein daalti hai.
  • Har channel ke workers queues se uthate hain aur providers ko call karte hain; failures backoff ke saath retry; permanent failures dead-letter queue mein.
  • Guarantees: at-least-once delivery (bhejne se pehle persist) + double-send se bachne ke liye event ID se dedup. End-to-end exactly-once possible nahi.
  • Production-grade banane waale extras: device-token lifecycle, opt-outs, quiet hours, priority lanes (OTP ≫ marketing), analytics (sent → delivered → opened → clicked).

docs.title: Intuition: post office ka sorting room
docs.text: Ek company apni saari outgoing daak ek sorting room mein daalti hai. Clerks har chitthi ka address check karte hain aur dekhte hain ki receiver ne us tarah ki daak band karwayi hai ya nahi, use sahi tray mein daalte hain — speed post, courier, normal post — aur trays alag delivery partners apni speed se khaali karte hain. Courier deliver na kar paaye toh chitthi "retry" tray mein wapas. Urgent chitthiyan (OTPs!) alag tray mein jo hamesha pehle khaali hoti hai.

docs.title: Step 1 · Scope
docs.text:
Clarifying baatcheet

Tum: Kaunse channels? — Interviewer: Mobile push, SMS aur email. Tum: Real-time? — I: Soft real-time: OTPs seconds mein; baaki load mein thodi late chalegi. Tum: Devices? — I: iOS, Android, aur desktop browsers. Tum: Notifications trigger kaun karta hai? — I: Hamari backend services (orders, payments, social) aur scheduled marketing campaigns. Tum: Users opt out kar sakte hain? — I: Haan, har channel aur har category ke liye; transactional messages (OTP) band nahi ho sakte. Tum: Volume? — I: Roz ~30M push, ~5M SMS aur ~20M emails.

Functional: push/SMS/email bhejo; templates support karo; user settings maano; immediate aur scheduled sends; delivery status report karo. Non-functional: high reliability (koi notification na khoye), critical waalon ke liye low latency, spikes tak scalable (50M users ko sale announcement), jahan ho sake duplicates nahi.

docs.title: Estimates
docs.text:
Channel Per din Avg/s Peak (campaign bursts) Push 30 M ~350 broadcast pe 50K+/s SMS 5 M ~60 ~2K/s (provider-limited) Email 20 M ~230 newsletter pe 10K+/s

Averages bahut chhote hain; design ko bursts aur provider limits chalate hain → queues.

docs.title: Step 2 · Har channel kaise kaam karta hai
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph iOS
      P1[Provider<br/>hamara backend] -->|"device token + payload"| APNS[APNs] --> D1[iPhone]
    end
    subgraph Android
      P2[Provider] -->|"registration token + payload"| FCM[FCM] --> D2[Android phone]
    end
    subgraph SMS
      P3[Provider] --> GW["SMS gateway<br/>(Twilio, MSG91…)"] --> D3[Phone]
    end
    subgraph Email
      P4[Provider] --> ES["Email service<br/>(SES, SendGrid…)"] --> D4[Inbox]
    end

Push (iOS / APNs):

  • Device token — APNs har app install ko ek unique identifier deta hai; app login/startup pe ise hamare backend ko bhejta hai.
  • Payload — JSON, jaise:
{
  "aps": {
    "alert": { "title": "Order shipped 📦", "body": "Aapka kurta raste mein hai. Abhi track karein." },
    "badge": 1,
    "sound": "default"
  },
  "order_id": "OD-77812"
}
  • Hamara server APNs pe authenticate karta hai (token-based JWT ya certificate) aur (device token, payload) bhejta hai.

Push (Android / web — FCM): same idea, FCM registration token ke saath. (Kuch regions mein FCM available nahi — jaise mainland China — wahan vendors ki apni push services use hoti hain.)

SMS: third-party gateways. India mein commercial SMS ke liye DLT registration bhi chahiye (pre-approved sender IDs aur templates) — ek asli-duniya ka constraint jo templates ko zaroori bana deta hai.

Email: commercial email service deliverability (SPF/DKIM/DMARC setup, IP reputation, bounce handling) aur analytics deti hai — apne SMTP servers chalane se kahin better.

docs.title: Contact info jama karna
docs.text:
Sign-up / app install / login pe app phone, email aur device tokens ek API ko bhejta hai jo unhe store karti hai.

users(user_id PK, email, phone_e164, country_code, created_at)
devices(device_id PK, user_id FK, platform /* ios|android|web */, push_token,
        app_version, last_seen_at, is_active)
-- ek user ↔ kai devices

Tokens badalte aur expire hote hain (app reinstall, OS update). Jab APNs/FCM bole token invalid hai, use inactive mark karo; har app start pe bhi tokens refresh karo.

docs.title: Pehla draft (aur yeh kaafi kyun nahi)
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S1[Order service] --> NS[Notification server]
    S2[Payment service] --> NS
    S3[Campaign scheduler] --> NS
    NS --> APNS[APNs] & FCM[FCM] & SMS[SMS gateway] & EM[Email service]

Problems:

  • Single point of failure — ek notification server.
  • Scale karna mushkil — DB, cache aur sending sab ek box mein; alag-alag scale nahi kar sakte.
  • Performance bottleneck — HTML render karna aur slow providers ka wait request path ke andar sab block karta hai; spike use dabaa deta hai.
  • Ek slow provider saare channels rok deta hai (jaise SMS gateway timeouts push ko bhi atka dete hain).

docs.title: Behtar design
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S1[Order svc] & S2[Payment svc] & S3[Campaign scheduler] -->|"POST /v1/notifications"| LB{{LB}} --> NS["Notification service<br/>(stateless, kai)"]
    NS --> CACHE[(Cache:<br/>users, devices, settings, templates)]
    NS --> DB[(Notification DB:<br/>users, devices, settings, log)]
    NS --> QP[["Queue: push"]] & QS[["Queue: SMS"]] & QE[["Queue: email"]]
    QP --> WP[Push workers] --> APNS[APNs] & FCM[FCM]
    QS --> WS[SMS workers] --> GW[SMS gateway]
    QE --> WE[Email workers] --> ESV[Email service]
    WP & WS & WE -.->|"failed: retry"| QP & QS & QE
    WP & WS & WE --> LOG[(Notification log)]

Kya badla:

  • Notification service stateless aur horizontally scaled hai, load balancer ke peeche.
  • DB + cache users, devices, settings, templates rakhte hain — cached kyunki har send ko yeh chahiye.
  • Har channel ki ek queue — SMS provider outage sirf SMS queue atkaata hai; push aur email chalte rehte hain. Queues bursts bhi sokhti hain.
  • Har channel ke workers jobs uthate hain aur providers ko unki allowed rate pe call karte hain.

docs.title: Ek notification ka flow
docs.text:
1. Koi service user ID(s), template ID, data, aur channels/priority ke saath POST /v1/notifications call karti hai.
  2. Notification service caller ko authenticate aur request ko validate karti hai.
  3. User contact info, device tokens aur notification settings laati hai (cache → DB).
  4. Jin channels se user ne opt out kiya unhe hatati hai, rate limits lagati hai, template render karti hai.
  5. Notification ko log mein likhti hai (status = queued) aur har channel queue pe event publish karti hai.
  6. Workers events uthate hain, APNs/FCM/SMS/email call karte hain, aur status update karte hain (sent / failed).
  7. Providers devices tak deliver karte hain; delivery receipts aur opens/clicks events ki tarah wapas aate hain.
POST /v1/notifications
{
  "event_id": "order-shipped:OD-77812",          ← idempotency key
  "user_ids": [123456],
  "template": "order_shipped",
  "data": { "order_id": "OD-77812", "item": "kurta" },
  "channels": ["push", "email"],
  "priority": "transactional"                      ← vs "promotional"
}

docs.title: Reliability: koi notification kabhi na khoye
docs.text:
Bhejne se pehle persist karo. Caller ko acknowledge karne se pehle notification durable store (log DB) aur durable queue (replication waala Kafka/SQS) mein likhi jaati hai. Worker beech mein crash ho toh message dobara deliver hota hai aur retry hota hai.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> queued
    queued --> sending: worker ne uthaya
    sending --> sent: provider ne accept kiya
    sending --> retrying: timeout / 5xx
    retrying --> sending: backoff ke baad
    retrying --> dead_letter: max attempts
    sent --> delivered: delivery receipt
    delivered --> opened: user ne khola
    sending --> failed: invalid token / bounce

Retries: jitter ke saath exponential backoff (jaise 1s, 2s, 4s… N attempts tak). Retryable (timeouts, 5xx, throttling) aur permanent errors (invalid token, unsubscribed, hard bounce) mein fark karo — permanent waalon ko retry mat karo, aur kharab token/address saaf karo.

docs.title: Kya users ko same notification do baar milegi?
docs.text:
At-least-once delivery mein duplicates ho sakte hain — jaise worker push bhejta hai, phir queue ko ack karne se pehle crash, toh message dobara deliver. Third-party provider ke across exactly-once guarantee karna impossible hai, par duplicates ko rare bana sakte hain:

  • Har notification ke saath ek event ID (idempotency key).
  • Bhejne se pehle worker ek dedup store check karta hai (jaise Redis SET event_id:channel:user NX EX 86400). Key pehle se hai toh skip.
  • API khud idempotent: same event_id do baar post ho toh ek hi notification banti hai.
boolean firstTime = redis.set("sent:" + eventId + ":" + channel + ":" + userId, "1",
                              SetParams.setParams().nx().ex(86_400)) != null;
if (!firstTime) return;                 // pehle handle ho chuka → skip
provider.send(payload);                 // yahin crash hua toh ab bhi rare duplicate ho sakta hai

docs.title: Notification templates
docs.text:
Zyada tar notifications ka shape same hota hai. Placeholders waala template har message dobara banane se bachata hai, formatting consistent rakhta hai, aur (India mein SMS ke liye) waise bhi kanoonan zaroori hai.

template: order_shipped (en)
  push.title: "Order shipped 📦"
  push.body : "Your {{item}} is on the way. Track it now."
  email.subject: "Your order {{order_id}} has shipped"
  email.html: <layout> … {{item}} … <a href="{{track_url}}">Track</a> … </layout>
template: order_shipped (hi)
  push.body : "Aapka {{item}} raste mein hai. Abhi track karein."

Templates versions aur locales ke saath store karo; rendered tukde cache karo.

docs.title: Notification settings (preferences)
docs.text:
Users ko control hona chahiye ki unhe kya mile. Har user, har channel, har category ke liye store karo:

notification_settings(
  user_id   BIGINT,
  channel   VARCHAR(10),     -- push | sms | email
  category  VARCHAR(30),     -- transactional | social | promotions | reminders
  opted_in  BOOLEAN,
  quiet_from TIME NULL, quiet_to TIME NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, channel, category)
)

Queue karne se pehle settings check karo. Transactional messages (OTP, payment alerts) opt-outs bypass karte hain par sanity limits maante hain; promotional waale quiet hours aur local regulations maante hain.

docs.title: Rate limiting (users aur providers dono ki raksha)
docs.text:
• Per user: jaise din mein max 3 promotional pushes — zyada hue toh users notifications hi band kar dete hain (ya app uninstall).
  • Per provider: SMS gateways aur APNs/FCM ki throughput limits hain; workers unke neeche rehne ke liye token buckets (Chapter 4) use karte hain.
  • Per caller service: loop mein phasi ek buggy service users ko flood na kare.

docs.title: Priorities
docs.text: OTPs 5 crore users ke marketing blast ke peeche wait nahi kar sakte. Har priority ki alag queues (ya topics) rakho: transactional ke dedicated workers aur capacity, promotional bachi hui capacity se khaali hoti hai.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Sirf authenticated internal services (mTLS, service tokens, ya appKey/appSecret) notification API call kar sakein. Validate karo ki caller kisi template category ko bhej sakta hai ya nahi. Push payloads mein kabhi secrets ya poori PII mat daalo — woh lock screen pe dikhte hain.

docs.title: Monitoring & tracking
docs.text:
• Har channel ki queue depth / consumer lag — sabse key health signal. Lag badh raha hai → workers badhao ya provider check karo.
  • Provider error rates aur latency, invalid-token rates.
  • Funnel analytics: created → sent → delivered → opened → clicked, har template ke liye — product teams isi pe jeeti hain.
flowchart LR
    W[Workers] -->|"sent / failed"| EV[[Events stream]]
    PR["Providers<br/>(delivery receipts, bounces)"] --> EV
    APP["Apps<br/>(opened, clicked)"] --> EV
    EV --> AN[(Analytics store)] --> DASH[Dashboards / alerts]

docs.title: Final design
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    SV["Internal services<br/>+ campaign scheduler"] -->|"auth'd API calls"| LB{{LB}} --> NS[Notification service]
    NS --> RL{"Rate limiter<br/>+ settings check"}
    RL --> TPL[Template renderer]
    TPL --> LOGW[(Notification log)]
    TPL --> TQ[["transactional queues<br/>push · sms · email"]]
    TPL --> PQ[["promotional queues<br/>push · sms · email"]]
    TQ & PQ --> WK["Channel workers<br/>(dedup check · provider rate limit · retries)"]
    WK --> PROV["APNs · FCM · SMS gateway · Email service"]
    WK -.-> DLQ[["Dead-letter queue"]]
    WK & PROV --> EV[[Tracking events]] --> AN[(Analytics)]
    NS --> C[(Cache)] --> DB[(DB: users, devices,<br/>settings, templates)]

docs.title: Interviewer follow-ups
docs.text:
5 crore users ko ek push jaldi kaise bhejoge?

API request ke andar fan out mat karo. Campaign service ek campaign job banati hai; fan-out stage target segment ko pages mein padhta hai (jaise har page 10K user IDs) aur batched jobs enqueue karta hai; kai workers parallel bhejte hain, jahan ho sake provider batch APIs (FCM topics/multicast) use karke. Provider limits tak throttle karo; message urgent nahi toh seconds ki jagah minutes mein phailao; promotional lane se bhejo taaki OTPs late na hon.

Stale device tokens ka kya karoge?

Har app launch/login pe tokens refresh karo; last_seen_at store karo; jab APNs/FCM "unregistered/invalid token" bolein, device ko turant inactive mark karo; N mahine se na dikhe devices samay-samay pe purge karo. Mare hue tokens pe bhejna capacity barbaad karta hai aur sender reputation kharab kar sakta hai.

Phone offline tha isliye push fail hua. Retry karein?

Nahi — APNs/FCM khud offline devices ke liye store-and-forward karte hain (tumhare set kiye TTL/collapse key ke saath). Provider ne message accept kar liya toh hamara kaam khatam. Retry sirf tab jab provider call fail ho. Collapse keys use karo taaki online aane pe phone ko 3 alag stale pushes ki jagah latest "3 naye messages" mile.

Har user ke time zone mein kal subah 9 baje ka reminder kaise schedule karoge?

Scheduled notifications ko har user ke time zone se nikaale absolute UTC send time ke saath store karo. Ek scheduler (time-bucketed table ya delay queue) har minute jaagta hai, due notifications uthata hai aur normal pipeline mein daalta hai. Send time pe preferences dobara check karo — ho sakta hai user ne beech mein opt out kar diya ho.

Kya exactly-once delivery guarantee kar sakte hain?

End-to-end nahi: APNs ya SMS gateway ko message dene ke baad timeout aaye toh pakka nahi pata ki deliver hua ya nahi. Hume dedup ke saath at-least-once milta hai — pehle persist, idempotent API, har (event, channel, user) ki dedup key — jo duplicates ko rare banata hai par impossible nahi. SMS/OTP ke liye duplicate harmless hai; paise waali emails mein stable reference daalo taaki users repeat pehchan sakein.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — SMS workers ka size

SMS gateway har account pe 500 requests/s allow karta hai aur har call ~200 ms leti hai. 2-ghante ke peak mein 18 lakh OTP+transactional SMS bhejne hain. Kitne concurrent worker threads, aur kya gateway limit kaafi hai?

Solution. Zaroori rate = 1.8M / 7,200 s = 250 SMS/s — 500/s limit ke neeche ✓. Concurrency = rate × latency = 250 × 0.2 s = 50 in-flight calls; 2× bursts ke headroom ke saath, kuch worker instances mein ~100 threads.

Practice 2 — Settings check design karo

Promotional push sirf un users ko jaana chahiye jinhone push pe promotions opt in kiya hai, local quiet hours mein nahi hain, aur aaj ≥ 3 promotional pushes nahi mile. Decision order aur zaroori data likho.

Solution. (1) (user, push, promotions) ka settings lookup (cache) → opted_in? (2) user ka time zone + quiet hours → abhi allowed? nahi toh quiet hours khatam hone pe schedule; (3) Redis mein per-user daily counter promo:push:{user}:{date} → INCR karke 3 se compare (atomic); (4) tabhi enqueue. Saste checks pehle.

Practice 3 — Bug pakdo

Ek worker karta hai: provider ko bhejo → DB mein sent mark karo → queue message ack karo. Kis failure pe users ko duplicates milenge, aur kaise kam karoge?

Solution. Bhejne ke baad aur ack se pehle worker crash hua toh message dobara deliver hoga aur dobara jaayega. Bhejne se pehle check/set hone waali dedup key (SET NX) se kam karo, aur provider message IDs record karo. Ek chhoti window bachti hai (provider call aur dedup write ke beech crash) — notifications ke liye acceptable.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• APNs, FCM, SMS gateways aur email services kahan fit hote hain, aur device token kya hai — samjha sakta hoon.
  • Contact-info tables aur token lifecycle design kar sakta hoon.
  • Pehla draft kyun fail hota hai aur per-channel queues + workers kaise fix karte hain — samjha sakta hoon.
  • Ek notification ko poore flow se guzaar sakta hoon.
  • At-least-once + dedup, backoff ke saath retries, aur dead-letter queues samjha sakta hoon.
  • Templates, user settings, rate limits, priorities, security aur tracking design kar sakta hoon.

Aage: 11 · News Feed

docs.title: 11 · News Feed System Design karo
docs.text:
⏱ 45 min read 🔥 Top-5 sabse zyada poochha jaane waala; fan-out trade-off hi poora interview hai Book: Chapter 11

TL;DR

  • Do flows: publishing (post store karo, followers ke feeds mein baanto) aur retrieval (precomputed feed padho, post/user data se hydrate karo).
  • Fan-out on write (push): post ke time har follower ke feed cache mein post ID daalo → reads instant; lakhon followers waale accounts ke liye writes phat jaate hain.
  • Fan-out on read (pull): feed maangne pe banao — jinhe follow karte ho unke recent posts merge karke → writes saste, reads slow.
  • Hybrid (asli systems yahi karte hain): normal accounts ke liye push, celebrities ke liye pull, read time pe merge; inactive users ko push mat karo.
  • Feed cache sirf IDs rakhta hai (jaise har user ke last ~800 post IDs ka Redis sorted set); asli posts aur users apne caches se aate hain (hydration). Cursors se paginate karo, offsets se nahi.

docs.title: Intuition: akhbaar waala
docs.text:
Ek akhbaar waala 1,000 gharon ko do tarah serve kar sakta hai:

  • Har subah ghar pahunchao (push): depot pe har ghar ke akhbaar bundle karo aur daal do. Ghar pe padhna instant — par agar ek magazine ke 10 lakh subscribers hain, toh har baar chhapne pe depot doob jaata hai.
  • Logon ko stall pe aane do (pull): kuch pre-bundle nahi; har banda aate hi apna selection utha leta hai. Chhaapna free — par har visit lambi, khaaskar us bande ke liye jo 500 magazines follow karta hai.

Samajhdaar akhbaar waala normal akhbaar ghar pahunchata hai aur bahut popular magazine stall pe rakhta hai, jahan har koi aate hi copy utha leta hai. Yahi hybrid hai.

docs.title: Step 1 · Scope
docs.text:
Clarifying baatcheet

Tum: Follow model — mutual dost, ya one-way follows? — Interviewer: One-way follows, Instagram/X jaisa. Kuch accounts ke crore se zyada followers hain. Tum: Feed mein kya hai? — I: Jinhe follow karte ho unke posts: text, images, short videos. Tum: Order? — I: Abhi reverse-chronological; baad mein ranking aa sakti hai. Tum: Scale? — I: 25M DAU; users average ~300 accounts follow karte hain, max 7,500. Tum: Platforms? — I: Mobile apps aur web. Tum: Kitna fresh hona chahiye? — I: Naya post followers ke feeds mein kuch seconds mein dikhe; thoda stale chalega.

docs.title: Estimates
docs.text: Cheez Value Posts 25M DAU × 0.5 posts/din = 12.5M/din → ~150/s, peak ~500/s Feed loads 25M × 12 opens/din = 300M/din → ~3.5K/s, peak ~10K/s Fan-out writes (push, avg 300 followers) 150 posts/s × 300 = average 45K feed inserts/s Ek celebrity post (30M followers) Ek hi post ke 30M inserts ← yahi problem hai Feed cache 25M users × 800 IDs × ~16 B (ID + score) ≈ 320 GB

docs.title: Feed publishing
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    U[User] -->|"POST /v1/me/posts"| LB{{LB}} --> WS["Web servers<br/>auth · rate limit"]
    WS --> PS[Post service] --> PDB[(Post DB)] & PC[(Post cache)]
    WS --> FO[Fan-out service] --> FC[(News feed cache)]
    WS --> NS[Notification service]
  • Web servers user ko authenticate karte hain aur posting ko rate-limit karte hain (spam rokta hai).
  • Post service post persist karti hai (DB + cache).
  • Fan-out service post ID ko followers ke feeds mein dhakelti hai.
  • Notification service opt-in waale followers ko batati hai (Chapter 10).

docs.title: Feed retrieval
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    U[User] -->|"GET /v1/me/feed"| LB{{LB}} --> WS[Web servers] --> NF[News feed service]
    NF --> FC[(News feed cache:<br/>post IDs)]
    NF --> UC[(User cache)] & PC[(Post cache)]
    U -.->|images / video| CDN[(CDN)]

News feed service post IDs ki list padhti hai, phir unhe hydrate karti hai — author ka naam/avatar, text, media URLs, like counts — aur JSON return karti hai. Media khud CDN se stream hota hai.

docs.title: Fan-out on write vs fan-out on read
docs.text:
Fan-out on write (push) Fan-out on read (pull) Kaam kab hota hai Post ke time Read ke time Read latency ✅ Bahut tez — feed precomputed ❌ Slow — har request pe N timelines merge Write cost ❌ Har post pe O(followers); celebrity = lakhon writes ✅ O(1) — bas post store karo Barbaad kaam ❌ Un inactive users ko push jo kabhi padhte nahi ✅ Sirf active readers kharcha karte hain Freshness Near-real-time Real-time (maangne pe compute) Best for Normal users, read-heavy apps Celebrities, kam active users

Hybrid:

  • ≤ N followers waale users (maan lo 100K): followers ke feeds mein push.
  • Celebrities (> N followers): push mat karo. Read time pe unke recent posts laao aur merge karo.
  • Jo followers 30 din se active nahi unhe push skip karo; agli visit pe unka feed rebuild karo.
  • User ID pe consistent hashing (Chapter 5) feed-cache keys phailata hai aur hotspots kam karta hai.

docs.title: Fan-out service detail mein
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    PS[Post service] -->|"new post event<br/>(post_id, author_id)"| MQ1[[Queue]]
    MQ1 --> F["Fan-out service"]
    F -->|"1. follower IDs"| G[(Graph DB / follows store)]
    F -->|"2. filter: muted, blocked,<br/>inactive, settings"| UC[(User cache / DB)]
    F -->|"3. 1,000 follower IDs ke batches"| MQ2[[Fan-out queue]]
    MQ2 --> W1[Worker] & W2[Worker] & W3[Worker]
    W1 & W2 & W3 -->|"4. ZADD feed:{follower} post_id"| FC[(News feed cache<br/>Redis sorted sets)]
  1. Author ke follower IDs follows store se laao (graph DB, ya followee_id se keyed sharded follows table).
  2. Woh followers filter karo jinhone author ko mute/block kiya, jo inactive hain, ya jinhone yeh content na dekhne ka chuna.
  3. Followers ko batches mein todo aur enqueue karo — taaki 50K-follower post 50 independent jobs ban jaaye jo parallel process hon.
  4. Workers har follower ke feed cache mein post_id daalte hain.

Har user ke liye kya store hota hai: sirf (post_id, score) — post nahi. Bounded rakho: last ~800 entries. Users shaayad hi usse aage scroll karte hain; purane items zaroorat pe DB se rebuild ho sakte hain.

/** Fan-out worker: ek post ko followers ke ek batch ke feeds mein daalo (Redis sorted sets). */
void fanOut(long postId, long createdAtMs, List<Long> followerIds) {
    try (Pipeline p = jedis.pipelined()) {
        for (long f : followerIds) {
            String key = "feed:" + f;
            p.zadd(key, createdAtMs, Long.toString(postId));   // score = time (ya khud Snowflake ID)
            p.zremrangeByRank(key, 0, -801);                   // sirf naye 800 rakho
        }
        p.sync();
    }
}

Snowflake IDs achhe scores banti hain

Agar post IDs Snowflake IDs hain (Chapter 7), toh woh pehle se time-ordered hain — ID ko hi sort score aur pagination cursor bana do.

docs.title: Feed retrieval detail mein
docs.text:
1. Client GET /v1/me/feed?cursor=… call karta hai.
  2. News feed service feed:{me} se post IDs padhti hai: ZREVRANGEBYSCORE feed:{me} (cursor -inf LIMIT 0 20.
  3. Celebrity posts merge karo: user jin celebrities ko follow karta hai, har ek ke recent post IDs laao (har celebrity ka ek cached copy — uske saare followers share karte hain) aur score se merge karo.
  4. Hydrate: post cache se posts aur user cache se authors multi-get karo (miss pe DB).
  5. Jo delete ho gaya ya ab blocked hai use filter karo; next_cursor = aakhri item ka score ke saath response banao.
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant NF as News feed service
    participant FC as Feed cache
    participant CC as Celebrity posts cache
    participant PC as Post + user caches
    C->>NF: GET /v1/me/feed?cursor=X
    NF->>FC: ZREVRANGEBYSCORE feed:me (X, 20)
    NF->>CC: follow kiye celebrities ke recent posts
    NF->>NF: score se k-way merge, top 20 lo
    NF->>PC: MGET posts, MGET authors
    NF-->>C: 20 hydrated items + next_cursor

?page=3 ki jagah cursors kyun? Scroll karte hue upar naye posts aate rehte hain; offset pagination duplicates dikhayega ya items skip karega. Cursor ("ID X se purana sab kuch") stable hai.

docs.title: Cache layers
docs.text: Layer Kya rakhta hai Notes News feed Har user ke post IDs Bounded sorted sets; fan-out ka output Content Post bodies Hot posts alag hot tier mein (viral post lakhon baar padha jaata hai) Social graph Followers / following lists Fan-out aur "main kise follow karta hoon" (celebrity merge) dono use karte hain Action Kya maine is post ko like / repost / comment kiya? Heart icon sahi dikhane ke liye zaroori Counters Like, comment, repost, follower counts High-write; aksar approximate aur batched (Redis mein increment, samay-samay pe flush)

docs.title: Edits, deletes aur privacy
docs.text:
• Delete: post store mein post ko deleted mark karo; use lakhon feed caches mein dhoondhte mat phiro — hydration bas use gira deta hai.
  • Edit: feeds sirf IDs rakhte hain, toh agli hydration naya text apne aap dikhati hai.
  • Unfollow / block: read time pe turant filter; feed cache lazily saaf karo.
  • Private accounts: fan-out sirf approved followers ko; safety ke liye hydration pe permissions dobara check karo.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• Fan-out async hai — post store hote hi "published"; fan-out delays ka matlab feeds seconds peeche, posts khona nahi. Queues durable hain aur workers retry karte hain.
  • Feed cache kho gaya (node failure) toh maangne pe rebuild: followed accounts ke recent posts post store se kheencho (fallback ki tarah fan-out on read), phir repopulate.
  • Request coalescing aur rate limits se DB ko cache-miss storms se bachao (Chapter 1).

docs.title: Reverse-chronological se aage
docs.text: Ranked feeds candidate generation ke baad ek stage jodte hain: candidates jama karo (chronological feed + celebrity posts + recommendations), ML model se score karo (predicted engagement), re-rank karo, phir hydrate. Fan-out architecture wahi rehta hai — bas ab woh final order ki jagah candidates banata hai.

docs.title: Step 4 · Wrap-up — baaki ko scale karna
docs.text:
• Database: posts post_id se sharded; follows user se sharded; read replicas; access pattern ke hisaab se SQL vs NoSQL (Chapter 1).
  • Stateless web tier + aggressive caching; saare media ke liye CDN.
  • Multiple data centers, har region mein feed caches replicated post store se rebuild.
  • Queues se decouple (publishing, fan-out, notifications, counters).
  • Monitor: peak pe QPS, feed latency p99, fan-out lag (post se feed mein dikhne tak ka time), cache hit ratios.

docs.title: Interviewer follow-ups
docs.text:
4 crore followers waala celebrity post karta hai. Kya hota hai, step by step batao.

Post store hota hai. Author celebrity threshold ke upar hai, toh fan-out nahi hota; post ID celebrity ki apni "recent posts" list mein jud jaata hai (cached, replicated, bahut hot). Jab koi follower feed load karta hai, feed service uske precomputed feed ko uske follow kiye celebrities ke recent posts ke saath merge karti hai. Kharcha post time ke 4 crore writes se har feed load pe ek saste cached read pe aa jaata hai. Opt-in followers ko notifications throttling ke saath notification pipeline se jaati hain.

Celebrity threshold kaise chunoge?

Fan-out write cost vs read-time merge cost balance karo. Naapo: har post ka fan-out lag aur worker cost vs K celebrity lists merge karne se badhi feed latency. Typical thresholds das hazaar se lakhon followers ke beech hote hain. Posting frequency bhi dekho — din mein 100 baar post karne waala 100K-follower account hafte mein ek baar post karne waale 1M account se mehenga hai.

Ek user 7,500 accounts follow karta hai aur 3 mahine se app nahi khola. Wapas aane pe kya hota hai?

30 din inactivity ke baad humne use push band kar diya, toh uska feed cache stale/khaali hai. Wapas aane pe ek baar fan-out on read chalao: followed accounts ke recent posts laao (per-author recent-post caches se), merge karo, result ko uska feed cache bana do, aur push fan-out phir shuru. Baaki banne tak jaldi se pehla page dikha do.

Scale pe 'liked by you' aur sahi like counts kaise dikhaoge?

'Liked by you' (user, post) se keyed action cache se aata hai (ya user ke recent likes ka Bloom-ish set). Counts counter caches se: har like pe Redis mein increment, batches mein asynchronously persist. Real time mein exact counts zaroori nahi; bahut bade posts ke liye approximate/batched counters theek hain.

Feed cache mein sirf post IDs kyun?

Memory: ID ~8 bytes hai, hydrated post kilobytes — 800 posts × 25M users terabytes ho jaayenge. Consistency bhi: edits aur deletes hydration ke time turant lagu hote hain, lakhon feeds dobara likhe bina. Content post cache mein ek baar cached hai aur share hota hai.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — Fan-out cost

Normal users se roz 1M posts, median 200 followers (mean 400), aur 50 celebrities jo har din 5 baar post karte hain, average 20M followers. Pure push vs hybrid mein roz ke feed inserts nikalo.

Solution. Normal users: dono tarah 1M × 400 = 400M inserts/din. Push ke saath celebrities: 50 × 5 × 20M = 5B/din (saare normal traffic ka 12×!). Hybrid: celebrities 0 inserts — iski jagah followers ke reads 250 cached posts merge karte hain. Hybrid total 400M/din ≈ 4.6K inserts/s.

Practice 2 — Feed cache memory

40M active users, har ek ke 500 post IDs Redis sorted sets mein. Redis mein har entry ~64 bytes (member + score + skiplist overhead). Kitni memory? 70% utilisation pe 64 GB ke kitne nodes?

Solution. 40M × 500 × 64 B = 1.28 TB. Har node pe usable = 45 GB → ~29 nodes (replicas ke saath → ~58). 300 entries tak trim karna ya inactive users skip karna ise kaafi kam kar deta hai.

Practice 3 — Pagination bug

App GET /feed?page=2&size=20 use karti hai. Users shikayat karte hain ki scroll karte hue same post do baar dikhta hai. Samjhao aur fix karo.

Solution. Page 1 aur page 2 fetch karne ke beech upar naye posts aa gaye, sab kuch k positions neeche khisak gaya — toh page 2 page 1 ke aakhri k items se shuru hota hai. Cursor-based pagination use karo: next_cursor = aakhri item ka score/ID; agli request usse strictly purane items maangti hai.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• Publishing aur retrieval flows bana ke har service ka naam bata sakta hoon.
  • Fan-out on write vs read compare kar sakta hoon aur numbers ke saath hybrid samjha sakta hoon.
  • Fan-out service ke steps aur bounded ID-only feed cache describe kar sakta hoon.
  • Hydration, read time pe celebrity merge, aur cursor pagination samjha sakta hoon.
  • Paancho cache layers aur har ek kya rakhta hai bata sakta hoon.
  • Deletes, edits, blocks, inactive users aur cache loss handle kar sakta hoon.

Aage: 12 · Chat System

docs.title: 12 · Chat System Design karo
docs.text:
⏱ 50 min read 🔥 Top-5 sabse zyada poochha jaane waala; real-time + storage + ordering test karta hai Book: Chapter 12

TL;DR

  • Clients ko server-initiated delivery chahiye → polling ya long polling ki jagah WebSockets (bi-directional, persistent).
  • Services baanto: stateless (login, profiles, groups — load balancer ke peeche), stateful chat servers (har user ka WebSocket rakhte hain), aur third-party push (offline users ke liye APNs/FCM).
  • Service discovery (jaise ZooKeeper) login pe user ko ek healthy, paas waala chat server assign karti hai.
  • Messages wide-column / key-value store (Cassandra, HBase) mein: bahut zyada write volume, reads "chat ke latest N messages" jaise. Key = (chat_id, message_id), time-sortable IDs ke saath.
  • Har device ek last_seen_message_id rakhta hai → multi-device sync matlab "X ke baad ka sab do". Presence heartbeats + dosto ko pub/sub se.

docs.title: Intuition: telephone exchange
docs.text:
Purane telephone exchanges poori call ke liye do phones ke beech ek live line khuli rakhte the. Kisi ko baar-baar "kuch naya?" poochna nahi padta tha — jaise hi koi bolta, awaaz dono taraf behti. Agar phone kahin aur off the hook hota, operator message le leta aur baad mein ghanti bajata.

Chat server wahi exchange hai: har phone apne chat server se ek live line (WebSocket) rakhta hai; messages turant dono taraf behte hain; agar tum offline ho, toh push notification operator ka call-back hai, aur message tumhare reconnect hone tak storage mein intezaar karta hai.

docs.title: Step 1 · Scope
docs.text:
Clarifying baatcheet

Tum: 1:1, groups, ya dono? — Interviewer: Dono. Groups mein 256 members tak. Tum: Mobile, web ya dono? — I: Dono; ek user ek saath kai devices pe logged in ho sakta hai. Tum: Scale? — I: 80M DAU. Tum: Message types? — I: Abhi sirf text (64 KB tak). Media baad mein. Tum: Messaging ke alawa features? — I: Online/last-seen indicator, delivery aur read receipts, offline hone pe push notifications. Tum: History kitne time? — I: Chat history 2 saal rakho. Tum: End-to-end encryption? — I: Design ke scope mein nahi, par mention karo.

docs.title: Estimates
docs.text: Cheez Value DAU 80M; peak pe ~25% online → 20M concurrent WebSockets Messages 80M × 40/din = 3.2B/din → ~37K/s, peak ~100K/s Group fan-out average group 20 members → group messages deliveries ko ~20× badhate hain Storage 3.2B × ~150 B ≈ 480 GB/din → 2 saal ≈ 350 TB (+ replicas) Chat servers ek tuned server pe ~500K connections → sirf connections ke liye ~40 servers (headroom ke liye 2× chalao)

docs.title: Server receiver ko message push kaise karega?
docs.text: HTTP client-initiated hai. Sender seedha POST kar sakta hai (ya apne socket pe bhej sakta hai). Mushkil hissa hai receiver: server ko unhe push karna hai. Teen options:

docs.title: Option 1 · Polling
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    loop har kuch second
        C->>S: koi naya message?
        S-->>C: nahi (zyada tar)
    end
Simple, par barbaadi: zyada tar requests khaali lautti hain, aur latency = polling interval.

docs.title: Option 2 · Long polling
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: koi naya message? (khula rakho)
    Note over S: message aane tak ya ~30 s timeout tak wait
    S-->>C: message
    C->>S: agla long poll
Latency better, par: jo server connection pakde hai, zaroori nahi wahi sender ka message receive kare (stateless LB routing); server ko pata nahi chalta client disconnect hua ya nahi; inactive users bhi har timeout pe reconnect karte hain.

docs.title: Option 3 · WebSocket ✅
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Chat server
    C->>S: HTTP GET Upgrade: websocket
    S-->>C: 101 Switching Protocols
    Note over C,S: persistent, bi-directional connection
    S-->>C: message (server-initiated)
    C->>S: message
HTTP se shuru hota hai aur upgrade hota hai; ports 80/443 pe chalta hai toh firewalls paar kar leta hai; full-duplex. Bhejne aur paane dono ke liye isi ko use karo — ek connection, simple client.

docs.title: Service architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    U[Users] -->|"HTTP: login, profile, groups"| LB{{Load balancer}}
    LB --> API["Stateless API services<br/>auth · user profile · groups · service discovery"]
    U <-->|"WebSocket"| CS["Stateful chat servers"]
    CS --> PS[Presence servers]
    CS --> IDG[Message ID generator]
    CS --> Q[[Message sync queues]]
    Q --> KV[(Chat KV store)]
    CS --> PN["Push notification service<br/>→ APNs / FCM"]
    API --> SD[(ZooKeeper<br/>chat server registry)]
    API --> DB[(User / group DB + cache)]
Kind Components Notes Stateless Login/auth, user profiles, group management, service discovery LB ke peeche classic request/response; freely scale Stateful Chat servers Har client ek chat server se persistent connection rakhta hai; user tabhi server badalta hai jab woh fail ho Third-party Push notifications (APNs/FCM) Offline users ko naye messages ka pata aise chalta hai (Chapter 10)

Scalability: 20M connections pakadne waala ek giant server sapnon jaisa SPOF hai; hum connections ko kai chat servers mein shard karte hain, aur baaki sab stateless rakhte hain.

docs.title: Storage: kaunsa database?
docs.text:
Do tarah ka data:

  1. Generic data — users, profiles, settings, friend lists, groups. Replicas aur sharding ke saath relational DB theek hai.
  2. Chat history — unique hissa. Iski properties:
    • Bahut zyada write volume (WhatsApp/Messenger scale pe roz das-hazaaron crore messages).
    • Reads zyada tar recent: "chat kholo → latest 50 dikhao", phir kabhi-kabhi peeche scroll.
    • Access chat aur time se, content se kam hi (search alag index hai).
    • 1:1 chats ke liye read:write ratio lagbhag 1:1.

→ Chat se partitioned wide-column / key-value store (Cassandra, HBase, ScyllaDB). Aasaan horizontal scaling, bahut low latency, aur chat ke liye battle-tested (Facebook Messenger ne historically HBase use kiya; Discord Cassandra/ScyllaDB use karta hai).

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
-- 1:1 messages (pair se partition, taaki ek conversation saath rahe)
messages_1to1
  chat_id      (partition key)  = min(user_a, user_b) + ":" + max(user_a, user_b)
  message_id   (clustering key, DESC)   -- time-sortable
  from_user_id
  content
  created_at

-- group messages
messages_group
  group_id     (partition key)
  message_id   (clustering key, DESC)
  from_user_id
  content
  created_at

Message IDs unique aur time se sortable honi chahiye — chat mein ordering inhi pe depend karti hai. Sirf created_at kaafi nahi (same ms mein do messages). Options:

  • Global Snowflake ID (Chapter 7) — aasaan, globally roughly ordered.
  • Per-chat sequence (local ID generator): IDs ko sirf ek chat ke andar ordered hona hai, jo guarantee karna kahin aasaan hai (jaise har chat partition ka counter).

docs.title: Service discovery
docs.text:
User login karta hai toh kis chat server se connect kare? ZooKeeper (ya etcd/Consul) live chat servers ki registry unke load aur location ke saath rakhta hai; API best waala chunti hai (paas ka, kam load waala) aur uska address return karti hai.

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as User A
    participant LB as Load balancer
    participant API as API servers
    participant ZK as Service discovery
    participant CS2 as Chat server 2
    A->>LB: login
    LB->>API: authenticate
    API->>ZK: A ke liye best chat server?
    ZK-->>API: chat-2.ap-south (kam load)
    API-->>A: token + ws://chat-2...
    A->>CS2: WebSocket kholo

Ek session registry (Redis: user_id → {chat_server, device}) record karti hai ki har user abhi kahan connected hai, taaki doosre servers messages unhe route kar sakein.

docs.title: 1:1 message flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as User A
    participant CS1 as Chat server 1
    participant ID as ID generator
    participant Q as Sync queue (B)
    participant KV as KV store
    participant CS2 as Chat server 2
    participant B as User B
    participant PN as Push service
    A->>CS1: B ko bhejo Kal milte hain? (client_msg_id c42)
    CS1->>ID: agla message_id
    CS1->>Q: B ke liye enqueue
    CS1->>KV: message persist
    CS1-->>A: ack (c42 → message_id)
    alt B online hai
        Q->>CS2: deliver
        CS2->>B: WebSocket pe push
        B-->>CS2: delivered receipt
    else B offline hai
        Q->>PN: push notification bhejo
    end
  1. A apne WebSocket pe chat server 1 ko message bhejta hai, retries pe dedup ke liye ek client-generated ID (c42) ke saath.
  2. Chat server 1 message_id leta hai aur message persist karta hai (KV store) — source of truth.
  3. Message ko B ki message sync queue pe daalta hai (socho: B ka inbox).
  4. A ko ack karta hai (A ke UI mein ek tick ✓).
  5. B online hai (session registry bolti hai chat server 2) toh message B ke WebSocket pe deliver hota hai; B ka app ack karta hai → delivered (✓✓).
  6. B offline hai toh push notification service APNs/FCM alert bhejti hai; message storage mein intezaar karta hai.

docs.title: Multi-device sync
docs.text:
User B ke paas phone aur laptop hai. Har device apna cur_max_message_id rakhta hai — har chat ke liye usne dekha latest message ID. Ek naya message device ke liye "naya" hai agar:

  • recipient logged-in user hai, aur
  • message_id > us device ka cur_max_message_id.

Reconnect pe device poochta hai "meri chats ka cur_max_message_id ke baad ka sab kuch", KV store se laata hai, aur apna pointer update karta hai. Har device ka alag pointer hai, toh har ek apne aap catch up karta hai.

docs.title: Chhota group chat
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[User A] -->|group G ko message| CS[Chat server]
    CS --> QB[["sync queue: B"]] & QC[["sync queue: C"]] & QD[["sync queue: D"]]
    QB --> B[User B]
    QC --> C[User C]
    QD --> D[User D]

Chhote groups (≤ kuch sau) ke liye, message (ya uski ID) ko har member ki sync queue / inbox mein copy karo. Har recipient ko phir sab kuch ke liye sirf ek inbox dekhna hai — simple aur tez. Keemat hai har message ki N copies, jo 256 ke groups ke liye theek hai par 100K members waale channels ke liye nahi — wahan readers group ki apni message stream se pull karte hain (Chapter 11 jaisa hi push-vs-pull trade-off).

Receiving side pe ek user ke inbox mein kai senders aur groups ke messages order mein merge hokar aate hain.

docs.title: Online presence
docs.text:
Dost online ho toh hara dot, warna "last seen".

  • Login: WebSocket bante hi presence server KV store mein status = online, last_active_at = now set karta hai.
  • Logout: status = offline set.
  • Disconnects gande hain: mobile networks lagatar toot-te hain (lift, tunnel). Har jhatke pe offline/online flip karna noisy aur mehenga hai. Heartbeat use karo: client har ~5 s bhejta hai; ~30 s tak koi na aaye toh user offline mark karo.
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant P as Presence server
    C->>P: heartbeat
    Note over P: online
    C->>P: heartbeat (5 s baad)
    Note over C: network gaya (lift)
    C->>P: heartbeat (30 s ke andar reconnect)
    Note over P: ab bhi online — koi flap nahi
    Note over C: app band
    Note over P: 30 s tak heartbeat nahi → offline, last_seen = t

Status changes ka fan-out: pub/sub use karo — har user ka ek channel; dost usse subscribe karte hain (A→B, A→C…). A offline hota hai toh presence server ek baar publish karta hai aur subscribers ke chat servers update push karte hain. Chhoti friend lists/groups ke liye chalta hai; bade groups (jaise 50K members) ke liye presence push mat karo — sirf tab laao jab user group ya kisi member ki profile khole.

docs.title: Receipts: sent ✓, delivered ✓✓, read 🔵
docs.text:
• Sent: server ne message persist kiya (sender ko ack).
  • Delivered: recipient ke device ne receive ack kiya → server status update karke sender ko batata hai.
  • Read: recipient ne chat kholi → device bhejta hai "message_id X tak padh liya" (ek event kai messages cover karta hai). Groups mein har member ka track karo aur aggregate karo ("12 ne padha").

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• Chat server mar gaya: clients band WebSocket notice karte hain, service discovery se naya server maangte hain, reconnect karte hain, aur cur_max_message_id se resync — kuch nahi khota kyunki messages ack se pehle persist hue the.
  • Message retry: sender ko ack na mile toh same client_msg_id ke saath dobara bhejta hai; server dedup karta hai → duplicates nahi.
  • Ordering: chat ke andar message_id se order; client late aane waale messages ko sahi jagah daal deta hai.
  • Queue backlog / slow consumers: sync queues durable hain; recipients reconnect pe catch up karte hain.

docs.title: End-to-end encryption (mention)
docs.text: E2EE (Signal protocol, WhatsApp use karta hai) ke saath messages sender ke device pe un keys se encrypt hote hain jo sirf recipient devices ke paas hain. Server ciphertext store aur forward karta hai — content padh, search ya moderate nahi kar sakta, aur multi-device sync ke liye per-device keys chahiye. Upar ka architecture ab bhi chalta hai; bas payloads opaque ho jaate hain.

docs.title: Interviewer follow-ups
docs.text:
WebSockets ki jagah long polling kyun nahi?

Long polling chalta hai par hamare scale pe kamiyan hain: connections lagatar dobara bante hain (har message aur har timeout pe), jo server client ka poll pakde hai woh shayad sender ka message receive karne waala na ho (extra routing chahiye), aur disconnects detect karna mushkil. WebSockets har device ka ek persistent full-duplex connection dete hain — 20M concurrent users ke liye kam latency aur overhead.

Chat server 1 se message us user tak kaise route karoge jo chat server 7 pe connected hai?

Session registry (user_id → chat server(s)) mein recipient dekho, phir internal message bus se bhejo — jaise har chat server apni queue/topic consume kare, ya servers internal RPC se baat karein. Recipient se partitioned Kafka topics, ya har chat server ka Redis pub/sub channel, common choices hain.

Chat mein message order kaise guarantee karoge?

Aisi IDs do jo chat ke andar strictly badhti hon — jaise chat own karne waale partition ka per-chat sequence number — aur clients usi se sort karein. Chats ke across global ordering zaroori nahi. Snowflake IDs globally roughly ordered hain par servers ke across kuch ms ulat sakti hain; per-chat sequences isse bachate hain.

Ek group mein 1,00,000 members hain. Kya badlega?

Har member ke inbox mein message copy karna band karo (har message pe 100K writes). Message group ki stream mein ek baar store karo; members group kholne pe recent messages pull karte hain, aur poore message ki jagah halka notification/badge milta hai. Presence ya typing indicators fan out mat karo; kaun post kar sakta hai use rate-limit karo (announcement-style channels).

Message search kaise jodoge?

KV store "chat ke latest messages" ke liye optimised hai, text search ke liye nahi. Messages ko (asynchronously) user se partitioned search index (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch) mein stream karo, aur har user ke liye query karo. E2EE ke saath server-side search impossible hai — search device pe uski local copy pe chalta hai.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — Chat-server fleet ka size

Peak pe 35M concurrent connections. Ek chat server 60% CPU pe 400K connections sambhalta hai. 3 regions mein traffic 50/30/20 bata hai aur har region mein N+2 redundancy chahiye. Har region mein kitne servers?

Solution. Region connections: 17.5M, 10.5M, 7M → ÷ 400K = 44, 27, 18 servers → har ek +2 → 46, 29, 20 (total 95). Ek region ke doosron pe fail over hone ki capacity bhi plan karo.

Practice 2 — Multi-device catch-up

Chat X ke liye B ke phone ka cur_max_message_id = 9100 aur laptop ka = 9180. Messages 9101–9200 hain. Phone reconnect karta hai. Kya fetch hoga, aur laptop ka kya?

Solution. Phone chat X mein message_id > 9100 query karta hai → 100 messages, pointer 9200 pe update. Laptop pe tab tak asar nahi jab tak woh reconnect na kare/live messages na paaye; woh > 9180 laayega → 20 messages. Read receipts per-user hain, toh phone "9200 tak read" mark kare toh laptop ka UI sync event se unread badges saaf kar sakta hai.

Practice 3 — Presence traffic

20M online users har 5 s heartbeat bhejte hain. Heartbeat QPS kya hai? Kaise kam karoge?

Solution. 20M / 5 = 4M heartbeats/s — kaafi zyada. Kam karne ke tareeke: heartbeats existing WebSocket pe bhejo (naye connections nahi), chat server kisi bhi message ko heartbeat maane, interval 15–30 s aur timeout 60–90 s karo, aur presence store sirf state badalne pe (online ↔ offline) update karo, har heartbeat pe nahi.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• Polling, long polling aur WebSockets compare karke WebSockets justify kar sakta hoon.
  • Stateless, stateful aur third-party services alag kar sakta hoon aur service discovery samjha sakta hoon.
  • Messages ke liye wide-column/KV store justify kar sakta hoon aur 1:1 aur group data model design kar sakta hoon.
  • Pata hai message IDs time-sortable kyun honi chahiye aur unhe banane ke do tareeke.
  • 1:1 delivery (online/offline), multi-device sync, aur small-group fan-out samjha sakta hoon.
  • Heartbeats aur pub/sub se presence, receipts, aur failure recovery design kar sakta hoon.

Aage: 13 · Search Autocomplete

docs.title: 13 · Search Autocomplete System Design karo
docs.text:
⏱ 40 min read 🔥 Data structures + offline/online split test karta hai Book: Chapter 13

TL;DR

  • User ne jo type kiya usse shuru hone waali top-k sabse popular queries do — < 100 ms mein, har keystroke pe.
  • Core structure: trie. Lookups ko O(prefix length) banao: (1) prefix length cap karke aur (2) har node pe top-k completions cache karke.
  • Do systems mein baanto: data-gathering service (offline: query logs → aggregate → trie ko weekly/daily rebuild) aur query service (online: memory/cache mein read-only trie).
  • Traffic kam karo: client pe debouncing, browser caching (Cache-Control), aur logs ki sampling.
  • Trie ko prefix pe shard karke scale karo, ek shard map ke saath jo letters ki uneven frequency balance kare. Kharab suggestions ek filter layer se hatao.

docs.title: Intuition: chaiwala jo tumhara order jaanta hai
docs.text:
Tum apni roz ki chai ki tapri pe jaake bolte ho "ek ad—" aur chaiwala pehle se adrak chai daal raha hota hai, kyunki "ad" se shuru karne waale zyada tar log wahi maangte hain. Woh har baar poora menu nahi sochta; usne har shuruaat ka sabse popular ant yaad kar rakha hai. Aur woh yaad dheere-dheere update karta hai — hafton mein, jaise taste badalta hai — har customer ke saath nahi.

Yahi design hai: har prefix ke liye pehle se nikaale "sabse popular completions", history se samay-samay pe refresh.

docs.title: Step 1 · Scope
docs.text:
Clarifying baatcheet

Tum: Sirf query ki shuruaat se match, ya kahin bhi? — Interviewer: Sirf shuruaat se (prefix match). Tum: Kitne suggestions? — I: 10. Tum: Ranking kaise? — I: Poori query kitni baar search hui (popularity). Tum: Spell correction? Personalisation? — I: Abhi nahi; extensions ki tarah batao. Tum: Language? — I: English aur Roman script mein Hinglish/Hindi queries; Unicode ke liye baad mein design karo. Tum: Capitalisation aur special characters? — I: Sirf lower-case alphanumerics. Tum: Scale? — I: 30M DAU.

Requirements: tez (< 100 ms end-to-end, warna typing atki hui lagti hai) · relevant (results prefix se shuru) · popularity se sorted · scalable · highly available.

docs.title: Estimates
docs.text: Cheez Value Searches 30M DAU × 8 searches/din = 240M/din Har search pe requests ~6 (debounce ke baad har keystroke pe ek request, average query ~20 chars) QPS 240M × 6 / 10⁵ ≈ 14,400/s avg, ~30K/s peak Naya query data 240M × ~25 B = roz 6 GB logs; ~20% nayi unique queries → roz ~1.2 GB naya trie content

docs.title: Step 2 · High-level design
docs.text:
Do independent services:

  • Data gathering service — user queries jama karke unhe frequency table / trie mein aggregate karti hai. Offline, batch.
  • Query service — prefix diya, top 10 sabse frequent queries return. Online, read-only, tez.

docs.title: Naive version (yeh dekhne ke liye ki kyun fail hota hai)
docs.text:
Relational DB mein frequency table:

query frequency paneer tikka 41,200 paneer butter masala 37,900 pani puri 25,100 pasta 18,700 papad 6,300 
SELECT query FROM frequency_table
WHERE query LIKE 'pa%'
ORDER BY frequency DESC
LIMIT 10;

Hazaaron rows ke liye theek. Billions rows pe, har keystroke pe har LIKE 'pa%' match scan karke sort karna bahut slow. Prefix lookups ke liye bana structure chahiye.

docs.title: Trie (prefix tree)
docs.text:
• Root khaali string hai.
  • Har node ek character rakhta hai aur uske 26 (ya 36) tak children hote hain.
  • Har node ek prefix represent karta hai; jo nodes asli query poori karte hain woh uski frequency rakhte hain.
flowchart TB
    R(("root")) --> P((p))
    P --> PA((pa))
    PA --> PAN((pan)) & PAS((pas)) & PAP((pap))
    PAN --> PANE((pane)) & PANI(("pani"))
    PANE --> PANEE(("…paneer tikka: 41.2K<br/>…paneer butter masala: 37.9K"))
    PANI --> PANIP(("…pani puri: 25.1K"))
    PAS --> PASTA(("…pasta: 18.7K"))
    PAP --> PAPAD(("…papad: 6.3K"))

Naive top-k lookup:

  1. Prefix node tak neeche chalo — O(p), p = prefix length.
  2. Saare completions jama karne ke liye uska poora subtree traverse karo — O©, c = descendant nodes ki ginti.
  3. Sort karke top k lo — O(c log c).

Step 2 jaan leta hai: prefix "p" ke liye subtree poore trie ka bada hissa hai.

Do optimisations ise O(p) ≈ O(1) banati hain:

  1. Prefix length limit karo. Log suggestion chunne se pehle 50-character prefixes shaayad hi type karte hain. Maan lo 50 chars pe cap → node tak jaana O(1).
  2. Har node pe top-k cache karo. Har node apni precomputed top 10 completions ki list rakhta hai (frequencies ke saath). Lookup = node tak jao, uski list return — koi subtree traversal nahi.

Keemat: zyada memory (har query string apne saare prefixes ki top-k lists mein aati hai). Aam taur pe worth it — tez responses hi poora point hai.

Try karo — is widget ka har node apni top-k list rakhta hai:

final class AutocompleteTrie {
    private static final int K = 10;
    private static final class Node {
        final Map<Character, Node> kids = new HashMap<>();
        final List<Map.Entry<String, Long>> topK = new ArrayList<>();   // is prefix pe cached top-k
    }
    private final Node root = new Node();

    /** Offline build: aggregated table ke har (query, frequency) ke liye ek baar call. */
    void insert(String query, long freq) {
        Node n = root;
        offer(n, query, freq);
        for (char c : query.toCharArray()) {
            n = n.kids.computeIfAbsent(c, x -> new Node());
            offer(n, query, freq);
        }
    }

    private static void offer(Node n, String q, long f) {
        n.topK.add(Map.entry(q, f));
        n.topK.sort((a, b) -> Long.compare(b.getValue(), a.getValue()));
        if (n.topK.size() > K) n.topK.remove(K);
    }

    /** Online: O(prefix length). */
    List<String> suggest(String prefix) {
        Node n = root;
        for (char c : prefix.toCharArray()) { n = n.kids.get(c); if (n == null) return List.of(); }
        return n.topK.stream().map(Map.Entry::getKey).toList();
    }
}

docs.title: Data gathering service
docs.text:
Har search pe trie update karna (roz billions) bekaar aur mehenga hai: top suggestions minute-minute mein mushkil se badalte hain. Iski jagah batch pipeline:

flowchart LR
    LOGS[("Analytics logs<br/>query, timestamp<br/>append-only")] --> AGG["Aggregators<br/>(Spark / MapReduce)<br/>har hafte har query ka count"]
    AGG --> AD[("Aggregated data<br/>query · week · frequency")]
    AD --> WK["Workers<br/>trie banao"]
    WK --> TDB[("Trie DB<br/>(serialized trie / KV)")]
    TDB --> TC[("Trie cache<br/>(in-memory, read-only)")]
  1. Analytics logs — searches ke raw, append-only records (query, timestamp). Indexed nahi.
  2. Aggregators — samay-samay pe logs ko (query, time-window, frequency) mein roll up karte hain. Kitni baar, product pe depend: zyada tar search ke liye weekly theek; Twitter-style trending ko near-real-time chahiye (neeche dekho).
  3. Workers — aggregated data se asynchronously naya trie banate hain aur Trie DB mein store karte hain.
  4. Trie cache — distributed cache jo tez reads ke liye trie memory mein rakhta hai; har rebuild ke baad DB ka snapshot leke refresh.

Trie kahan store karein?

  • Document store — poore trie (ya har shard) ko snapshot blob ki tarah serialise karo, jaise MongoDB/S3 mein. Atomically swap karna aasaan.
  • Key-value store — har prefix → node data (top-k list) map karo. Har trie node ek key ban jaata hai: "pa" → ["paneer tikka", …]. Lookups ek GET ban jaate hain. Sharding aur caching ke liye bhi bahut convenient.
key (prefix) value (top-k) p paneer tikka, paneer butter masala, pani puri, pasta, … pa paneer tikka, paneer butter masala, pani puri, pasta, papad pan paneer tikka, paneer butter masala, pani puri pas pasta

docs.title: Query service
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser / app
    participant LB as Load balancer
    participant Q as Query service
    participant TC as Trie cache
    participant TDB as Trie DB
    B->>LB: GET /autocomplete?q=pan
    LB->>Q: forward
    Q->>TC: get("pan")
    alt cache hit
        TC-->>Q: [paneer tikka, paneer butter masala, pani puri]
    else miss
        Q->>TDB: get("pan")
        TDB-->>Q: top-k
        Q->>TC: fill
    end
    Q-->>B: suggestions (Cache-Control: max-age=3600)

Ise bijli jaisa tez banana:

  • Page se AJAX / fetch — full-page reloads nahi.
  • Client pe debounce: aakhri keystroke ke ~100–150 ms baad bhejo, aur ab bekaar ho chuki in-flight requests cancel karo.
  • Browser caching: prefix ke suggestions dheere badalte hain, toh Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600 ke saath respond karo — repeat prefixes browser khud answer karta hai (Google bhi kuch aisa karta hai).
  • Data sampling: full scale pe har query log karna processing mein bahut mehenga; N mein se 1 log karna bhi popularity sahi pakad leta hai.

docs.title: Trie operations
docs.text:
• Create — workers aggregated data se banate hain.
  • Update — ya toh (1) samay-samay pe rebuild karke naya trie swap karo (preferred), ya (2) individual nodes in place update karo — aur phir har ancestor ki top-k list bhi update karni padegi (mehenga; sirf chhote tries ke liye theek).
  • Delete — nafrat bhare, hinsak, sexually explicit ya khatarnak suggestions turant gayab hone chahiye, agle weekly rebuild pe nahi. Trie cache ke aage ek filter layer lagao jo blocklisted results gira de; agle rebuild pe unhe trie se physically hatao.
flowchart LR
    API[Query service] --> F{{"Filter layer<br/>(blocklist rules)"}} --> TC[(Trie cache)]

docs.title: Storage scale karna
docs.text:
Jab trie ek server se bada ho jaaye, prefix se shard karo:

  • Naive: 2 shards a–m aur n–z; 26 shards = har pehle letter ka ek; 26 se aage doosre letter pe shard (aa–ag, ah–an, …).
  • Problem: letters barabar use nahi hote — English mein s se shuru hone waale words x se kahin zyada hain. Barabar-letter ranges hot, uneven shards banati hain.
  • Fix: historical distribution analyse karo aur ek shard map manager (lookup DB) use karo jo ranges ko shards pe aise map kare ki har ek pe milta-julta load ho — jaise s akela ek shard, jabki u–z ek share karein.
flowchart LR
    Q[Query service] -->|"'pan' kis shard pe?"| SM[(Shard map manager)]
    SM -->|"shard 7"| Q
    Q --> S7[(Trie shard 7)]

docs.title: Step 4 · Wrap-up — extensions
docs.text:
Kai languages (Hindi, Tamil, Japanese…) kaise support karoge?

26-letter alphabet ki jagah trie nodes mein Unicode characters store karo (children array nahi, map ban jaate hain). Input normalise karo (Unicode NFC, jahan lagu ho lower-casing). Roman-script Hinglish ke liye transliteration variants ("paneer"/"panir") ko synonyms ki tarah merge karna pad sakta hai.

Har desh ke alag top queries?

Region-filtered logs se har desh/region ke alag tries banao, aur unhe un users ke paas CDNs/edges pe rakho. User locale se requests route karo.

Trending (real-time) queries kaise support karoge — jaise breaking news?

Weekly rebuilds 10 minute pehle phooti query nahi pakad sakte. Options: streaming pipeline (Kafka → Flink/Spark Streaming) jo sliding windows mein recent queries gine; recent queries ko zyada weight do (time-decayed scores); ek chhota real-time "trending" trie rakho jo query time pe main trie ke results ke saath merge ho. Sharding se working set kam karo.

Personalisation kaise jodoge?

Global suggestions ko user ki apni recent searches (per user store, chhoti) aur context (location, din ka time) ke saath blend karo. Query service dono laake re-rank karti hai — global trie wahi rehta hai.

Typos ka kya — 'panner' pe bhi 'paneer' suggest hona chahiye?

Prefix tries exact-match hain. Fuzzy matching jodo: edit distance 1–2 ke andar ke prefixes se trie query karo (trie pe bounded search), ya ek spelling-correction model rakho jo pehle prefix ko rewrite kare. Mehenga hai — sirf tab lagao jab exact prefix kam results de.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — Top-k caching ki memory

Ek trie mein 50M nodes hain. Har node apni top 10 completions ko 8-byte query IDs plus 8-byte frequencies ki tarah cache karta hai. Cached lists kitni memory jodti hain?

Solution. 50M × 10 × 16 B = 8 GB — plus query-ID → string dictionary jo ek baar store hoti hai. Manageable, aur sharding ise aur todti hai. (Har list mein poori strings rakhne se 5–10× zyada ho sakta hai.)

Practice 2 — Browser cache ki bachat

Users har search pe average 6 prefixes type karte hain, aur 40% prefixes woh hote hain jo us user ne pichle ek ghante mein maange the. 1-ghante browser cache ke saath server QPS kitna girega?

Solution. 40% requests browser serve karta hai → server QPS ~14.4K se ~8.6K/s average. Debouncing ke saath (jaise har search 6 → 4 requests), QPS ~5.8K/s tak gir sakta hai.

Practice 3 — Uneven shards

6 shards hain aur pehle letter se traffic share: s 12%, c 9%, p 8%, m 7%, b 6%, t 6%, a 6%, d 5%, baaki 41% 18 letters mein barabar. Balanced split propose karo.

Solution. Target ≈ har shard 16.7%. Ek assignment: S1 = {s, a} 18%; S2 = {c, p} 17%; S3 = {m, b, i, l} 7+6+2.3+2.3 ≈ 17.6%; S4 = {t, d, f, g, h, k} 6+5+2.3×4 ≈ 20%; S5 aur S6 bache 12 letters baant-te hain (~27% → har ek ~13.7%). Perfect nahi — S4 garam chalta hai, toh uska ek chhota letter S5 pe le jao — phir real data se tune karo. Shard map manager jo bhi ranges bane unhe store karta hai.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• Requirements bata sakta hoon aur per-keystroke requests ke liye QPS estimate kar sakta hoon.
  • SQL LIKE approach kyun fail hota hai aur trie kaise kaam karta hai — samjha sakta hoon.
  • Do optimisations (prefix cap + cached top-k) laga ke resulting complexity bata sakta hoon.
  • Data-gathering pipeline aur query service bana sakta hoon, aur updates batch kyun hote hain samjha sakta hoon.
  • Trie storage options (snapshot vs prefix→top-k KV), update/delete strategies aur filter layer pata hai.
  • Shard map ke saath prefix se shard kar sakta hoon, aur languages, regions, trending aur typos discuss kar sakta hoon.

Aage: 14 · YouTube

docs.title: 14 · YouTube Design karo
docs.text:
