⏱ 50 min read 🔥 Bada, open-ended — upload pipeline + CDN cost pe focus karo Book: Chapter 14

TL;DR

  • Do bade flows: upload (client → object storage → transcoding pipeline → CDN + metadata) aur streaming (client ← sabse paas ka CDN edge, adaptive bitrate).
  • Pre-signed URL se seedha blob storage pe upload karo; badi files ko chunks mein todo taaki upload parallel aur resumable ho.
  • Transcoding tasks ka ek DAG hai (inspect, kai resolutions/codecs mein encode, thumbnails, watermark, audio), jo queues se workers pe schedule hote hain.
  • HLS/DASH se stream: video kuch-second ke segments mein kai bitrates pe kat-ta hai; player bandwidth badalne pe quality switch karta hai.
  • Sabse bada bill CDN egress hai. CDN se sirf popular videos, long tail apne storage se; kam dekhe jaane waale videos lazily encode; content regionally rakho.

docs.title: Intuition: film distributor
docs.text:
Ek filmmaker distributor ko ek master print deta hai. Distributor alag formats mein copies banata hai (IMAX, 2K, dubbed version, trailer, poster), print mein damage check karta hai, aur copies darshakon ke paas waale cinemas tak bhejta hai. Blockbusters har cinema mein jaati hain; art-house film sirf kuch mein, aur koi maange toh godown se mangwayi jaati hai.

Upload = master print dena. Transcoding = saare formats banana. CDN = cinemas. Cost control = art-house films har multiplex mein na bhejna.

docs.title: Step 1 · Scope
docs.text:
Clarifying baatcheet

Tum: Long-form, short vertical clips, ya live? — Interviewer: Long-form aur short clips. Live scope se bahar. Tum: Viewers kahan hain, aur kaunse networks pe? — I: Zyada tar India aur South-East Asia, bahut saara patchy mobile data pe. Tum: Kitna bada? — I: Roz 20M viewers, har ek ~40 minute dekhta hai; kisi bhi din ~2% kuch upload karte hain. Tum: Creators kya upload karte hain? — I: Phone aur camera files, zyada tar formats mein, 4 GB tak. Tum: Kis quality mein stream karein? — I: Abhi 144p se 1080p. Tum: Storage aur CDN banayein ya khareedein? — I: Cloud object storage aur commercial CDN use karo. Tum: Paid/premium content? — I: Thoda — batao kaise protect karoge.

Focus: tez uploads, smooth streaming, quality switching, kam infrastructure cost, high availability, scalability, reliability.

docs.title: Estimates
docs.text:
Cheez Value Uploads DAU ka 2% roz 1 video → 400K videos/din (~5/s) Raw upload size avg 400 MB → roz 160 TB originals Stored renditions saari resolutions milake original ka ~1.5× → roz ~240 TB aur Watch volume 20M × 40 min = roz 800M minutes; ~2.5 Mbps ≈ 19 MB/min pe → roz ~15 PB egress CDN cost $0.01–0.02 per GB pe → roz $150K–300K ← sabse bada kharcha

Yeh numbers pehle hi bata dete hain ki deep dive kahan jaana chahiye: transcoding pipeline (correctness + throughput) aur CDN cost.

docs.title: Step 2 · High-level design
docs.text:
Cloud building blocks pe tiko:

  • Original aur transcoded videos ke liye blob/object storage (S3/GCS).
  • Streaming ke liye CDN.
  • Apne: API servers, metadata DB + cache, transcoding pipeline.
flowchart LR
    C["Client<br/>(phone · browser · TV)"] -->|"video stream"| CDN[(CDN)]
    C -->|"baaki sab:<br/>feed, upload URL, metadata,<br/>sign-in, likes"| API[API servers]
    API --> MDB[(Metadata DB)] & MC[(Metadata cache)]

docs.title: Upload flow
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    U[User] -->|"1. upload URL maango"| API[API servers]
    API -->|"2. pre-signed URL"| U
    U -->|"3. bytes upload (chunked, resumable)"| OS[(Original storage)]
    U -->|"4. title, description, tags"| API --> MDB[(Metadata DB + cache)]
    OS -->|"5. new upload event"| TP["Transcoding pipeline"]
    TP --> TS[(Transcoded storage)]
    TS --> CDN[(CDN)]
    TP -->|"6. done event"| CQ[[Completion queue]] --> CH["Completion handler"]
    CH -->|"status = ready,<br/>rendition URLs"| MDB
    CH -.-> N["Uploader ko notify"]

Do cheezein parallel mein hoti hain:

a) Asli video upload

  1. Client API se upload URL maangta hai. API ek pre-signed URL deti hai — time-limited URL jo ek specific object ko seedha object storage mein likhne ki permission deta hai. Hamare API servers gigabytes ko chhoote bhi nahi.
  2. Client original storage mein upload karta hai.
  3. "New upload" event transcoding pipeline chalata hai: video kai formats/resolutions mein badalta hai.
  4. Transcoded files transcoded storage mein aati hain aur CDN tak jaati hain / CDN unhe kheenchta hai.
  5. Transcoding khatam hone pe event completion queue pe jaata hai; completion handlers metadata DB/cache update karte hain (status = ready, rendition URLs, duration, thumbnails) aur uploader ko batate hain.

b) Metadata update

File upload hote hue client title, description, tags, visibility waghera API ko bhejta hai, jo unhe metadata DB aur cache mein likhti hai.

docs.title: Streaming flow
docs.text:
Streaming ka matlab player kuch seconds download karke shuru ho jaata hai aur dekhte hue laata rehta hai — pehle poora download nahi. Yeh streaming protocols pe tika hai:

Protocol Notes HLS (HTTP Live Streaming, Apple) Sabse zyada supported; .m3u8 playlists + segments MPEG-DASH Open standard; same idea, .mpd manifest Microsoft Smooth Streaming, Adobe HDS Purane / niche

Adaptive bitrate (ABR) streaming kaise kaam karta hai:

sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Player
    participant CDN as CDN edge (sabse paas)
    P->>CDN: GET master.m3u8
    CDN-->>P: renditions: 240p@400kbps, 480p@1Mbps, 720p@2.5Mbps, 1080p@5Mbps
    P->>CDN: GET 720p/segment_001.ts (4 s)
    P->>CDN: GET 720p/segment_002.ts
    Note over P: bandwidth gira (train tunnel mein)
    P->>CDN: GET 240p/segment_003.ts
    Note over P: bandwidth wapas aaya
    P->>CDN: GET 720p/segment_004.ts

Videos har resolution ke liye 2–6 second ke segments mein kat-te hain; ek manifest unhe list karta hai. Player throughput aur buffer level naapta hai aur agle segment ka bitrate chunta hai — isliye buffering ki jagah beech video quality badalti hai. Segments plain HTTP files hain → CDNs ke liye perfect.

docs.title: Transcode kyun karna?
docs.text:
• Raw video bahut bada hota hai — high-bitrate camera footage ka ek ghanta saikdon GB ho sakta hai.
  • Devices aur browsers alag formats/codecs support karte hain.
  • Networks alag hain — chalti train mein 4G waale ko 360p chahiye; fibre waale ko 1080p+.
  • Mobile conditions beech video badalti hain → switch karne ke liye kai bitrates chahiye.

Terms: video file ek container hai (.mp4, .webm, .mov, .mkv) jisme codecs se encoded streams hote hain (video: H.264/AVC, H.265/HEVC, VP9, AV1; audio: AAC, Opus). Naye codecs (VP9, AV1) 30–50% kam bits mein milti-julti quality dete hain — CDN ka paisa bachta hai — par encode karne mein zyada CPU lagta hai aur device support chahiye.

docs.title: Transcoding DAG
docs.text:
Alag creators ko alag processing chahiye (thumbnails, watermarks, sirf HD vs SD…). Kaam ko tasks ke directed acyclic graph ki tarah model karo (Facebook ka SVE aur Netflix ki pipelines yahi idea use karti hain):

flowchart LR
    O[Original video] --> SPLIT[Split: video · audio · metadata]
    SPLIT --> INS[Inspect<br/>quality, corruption]
    INS --> E1[Encode 1080p] & E2[Encode 720p] & E3[Encode 480p] & E4[Encode 240p]
    INS --> TH[Thumbnails]
    INS --> WM[Watermark]
    SPLIT --> AE[Audio encode<br/>AAC / Opus]
    SPLIT --> MD[Metadata nikaalo<br/>duration, size, codec]
    E1 & E2 & E3 & E4 & AE --> PKG["Package<br/>HLS/DASH segments + manifest"]
    PKG --> ASM[Assemble + publish]
    TH & WM & MD --> ASM
  • Inspect — pakka karo ki video valid hai aur toota nahi.
  • Encode — har resolution/codec/bitrate rendition banao.
  • Thumbnails — auto-generated ya user ne upload kiye.
  • Watermark — pehchaan waali info overlay.

docs.title: Scale pe DAG chalana
docs.text:
Pipeline ko chaar roles ki tarah socho. Companies inhe alag naam deti hain; matter karta hai har ek ka kaam.

flowchart LR
    OS[(Original storage)] --> PL["① Planner<br/>video ke chunks,<br/>DAG chuno"]
    PL --> OR["② Orchestrator<br/>kaunse tasks<br/>ready hain, track karo"]
    OR --> DQ[["③ Dispatch queues<br/>priority & task type se"]]
    DQ --> W1[Encoder pool] & W2[Thumbnail pool] & W3[Packager pool]
    W1 & W2 & W3 --> SCR[(Scratch storage)]
    W3 --> OUT[(Transcoded storage)]
    W1 & W2 & W3 -.->|"task khatam"| OR

① Planner. Upload padhta hai, use GOP-aligned chunks mein kaat-ta hai (GOP — group of pictures — frames ka ek run jo keyframe se shuru hota hai aur khud decode ho sakta hai, toh har chunk independently encode ho sakta hai). Config se kaunsa DAG chalana hai yeh bhi chunta hai: naye creator ki 15-second clip ko chhota DAG mil sakta hai (360p + 720p + thumbnail); premium upload ko poori ladder, do codecs aur watermark. Chunks aur metadata scratch storage mein jaate hain taaki koi bhi task original dobara padhe bina retry ho sake.

② Orchestrator. DAG ka state rakhta hai: kaunse tasks ho gaye, kaunse inputs ka wait kar rahe hain, kaunse ready hain. Task khatam hone pe dependents ko ready mark karke dispatch ko deta hai. Kyunki har rendition ka har chunk apna task hai, 10-minute video saikdon chhote parallel jobs mein phail sakta hai.

③ Dispatch. Ready tasks queues mein wait karte hain jo priority se bati hain (paying creator ka upload bulk re-encode se pehle) aur task type se (encode tasks ko bade CPU/GPU boxes chahiye; thumbnails saste hain). Workers sirf un queues se kheenchte hain jinke liye bane hain — pull-based dispatch load ko naturally balance karta hai: idle worker bas agla task utha leta hai.

④ Worker pools. Stateless processes (encoders, thumbnailers, watermarkers, packagers) jo scratch storage se inputs padhte hain aur outputs wapas likhte hain. Spot/preemptible machines ke liye ideal: ek gayab ho jaaye toh uska task time out hota hai aur doosra worker utha leta hai.

/** Transcoding DAG chalao: tasks tab runnable jab unki saari dependencies khatam ho jaayein. */
void runDag(Map<String, List<String>> deps, ExecutorService workers) throws InterruptedException {
    Map<String, Integer> pending = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    Map<String, List<String>> dependents = new HashMap<>();
    deps.forEach((task, ds) -> {
        pending.put(task, ds.size());
        ds.forEach(d -> dependents.computeIfAbsent(d, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(task));
    });
    CountDownLatch done = new CountDownLatch(deps.size());
    Consumer<String>[] submit = new Consumer[1];
    submit[0] = task -> workers.submit(() -> {
        execute(task);                                   // encode / thumbnail / watermark …
        for (String next : dependents.getOrDefault(task, List.of()))
            if (pending.merge(next, -1, Integer::sum) == 0) submit[0].accept(next);
        done.countDown();
    });
    pending.forEach((t, n) -> { if (n == 0) submit[0].accept(t); });   // koi dependency nahi → abhi shuru
    done.await();
}

docs.title: Uploads aur processing tez banana
docs.text: Bottleneck Hum kya karte hain Kyun kaam karta hai Kamzor link pe ek bada upload Client file ko parts mein todta hai, kai ek saath upload karta hai, sirf fail hue parts retry, crash ke baad resume Toota connection ek part ka nuksaan, poori file ka nahi Upload endpoint ki doori Regional upload endpoints (aksar CDN POPs) bytes lete hain, phir backbone se storage tak Slow "last mile" leg chhota Stages ek-doosre ka wait Har stage ke beech queue (fetch → encode → package → publish) Har stage apne aap scale; slow stage sabko rokne ki jagah backlog banata hai Pehle play tak ka time Pehle chhota rendition set publish, baaki baad mein Viewers upload ke minutes mein dekh sakte hain

docs.title: Uploads aur content ki raksha
docs.text:
• Kaun kya upload kare: API authenticated user se jude exactly ek object key ke liye short-lived URL sign karti hai — koi kisi aur ka video overwrite nahi kar sakta.
  • Kaun kya dekhe: private aur paid videos expire hone waale signed CDN URLs/cookies se serve hote hain.
  • Premium content copy hone se rokna: segments encrypt karo (AES) aur keys DRM system se do (Android/Chrome pe Widevine, Apple pe FairPlay, Windows/TVs pe PlayReady); visible ya forensic watermarks jodo taaki leaks trace ho sakein.

docs.title: Paisa kahan jaata hai — aur kam kaise kharchein
docs.text:
Egress hi bill hai. Views long tail follow karte hain, toh popular aur unpopular videos ko alag treat karo:

Lever Bachat Trade-off Sirf head (popular videos) CDN edges pe; tail origin storage se Badi — zyada bytes head ke, zyada videos tail ke Tail video ke pehle viewer ko slow start Extra renditions lazily, jab video ko views milne lagein Jinhe koi nahi dekhta un videos ka encoding CPU aur storage Achanak hit pe HD aane mein thoda delay Popularity ke region ke hisaab se distribute Regional hit ko duniya bhar mein pre-position karne ka kharcha nahi Per-region analytics chahiye Popular videos ke liye efficient codecs (VP9/AV1) Har view pe 30–50% kam bytes Encoding kai guna mehengi; device support alag-alag ISPs ke andar apne edge caches (bahut bade scale pe) Sasti bandwidth, kam latency Ek bada infrastructure programme

Yeh sab achhe analytics pe tike hain: kya dekha ja raha hai, kahan, aur views kitni tezi se badh rahe hain.

docs.title: Jab cheezein fail hon
docs.text:
Jo failures retry ho sakte hain unhe un se alag karo jo nahi ho sakte:

  • Retry (idempotent, chunk-level): time out hua part upload; encode task jiska worker gayab ho gaya; scratch storage pe fail hua write. Tasks chunks pe kaam karte hain aur deterministic paths pe likhte hain, toh dobara chalana safe hai.
  • Retry mat karo: corrupt ya unsupported file, ya policy checks fail karne waala video — upload ko saaf reason ke saath failed mark karo aur creator ko batao.
  • Planner/orchestrator instance kho gaya: uska state (DAG aur task status) durable store mein hai, toh doosra instance resume kar leta hai.
  • Serving path: API servers load balancer ke peeche stateless; metadata cache aur DB automatic failover ke saath replicated (Chapters 1 aur 6); edge cache miss ya fail ho toh CDN origin pe fall back karta hai.

docs.title: Step 4 · Wrap-up — aur kya
docs.text:
• API tier scale karo — stateless, horizontal.
  • Metadata DB scale karo — replication + sharding (video ID se).
  • Live streaming — same building blocks (encode, package, CDN) par bahut kam latency targets, toh alag protocols (low-latency HLS, WebRTC), chhote segments, processing mein kam parallelism, aur alag failure handling chahiye (live pal ko "retry" nahi kar sakte).
  • Takedowns — copyright/abuse removals ko storage se content delete/block aur CDN caches invalidate karne padte hain.
  • Recommendations, comments, view counts — alag systems; view counts high-write counters hain (batched, real time mein approximate).

docs.title: Interviewer follow-ups
docs.text:
API servers se upload karne ki jagah pre-signed URL kyun?

Uploads bahut bade (GBs) aur slow hain. Unhe API servers se guzaarne se har ek ki bandwidth, memory aur connections minutes tak bandh jaayenge. Pre-signed URL client ko seedha object storage mein likhne deta hai (jo isi ke liye bana hai), jabki API ab bhi control karti hai ki kaun, kya, aur kab tak upload kar sakta hai.

User flaky mobile network pe 4 GB video upload karta hai. Kaise chalega?

Chunked, resumable uploads (jaise S3 multipart ya tus protocol se 8 MB parts). Client parts parallel upload karta hai, sirf fail hue parts retry karta hai, aur app restart ke baad server se poochta hai kaunse parts aa chuke aur aage badhta hai. Saare parts aane pe server unhe jodta hai (ya pipeline seedha GOP chunks process karti hai).

Kitne renditions banane chahiye, aur kab?

Typical ladder: 144p/240p/360p/480p/720p/1080p (+ capable sources ke liye 4K), ek ya do codecs mein. Naye upload ke liye pehle ek chhota tez set banao (jaise 360p + 720p H.264) taaki video jaldi live ho; baaki asynchronously jodo, aur AV1/VP9 sirf tab jab video popular saabit ho.

Kaunse videos CDN pe jaayein, kaise decide karoge?

Har region ke liye view-count predictions aur recent popularity use karo: top N% videos edges pe push/rakho, baaki origin se fetch hone do (chhote TTLs ke saath pull-through). Lagatar re-evaluate karo; viral videos view velocity ke basis pe jaldi promote hote hain.

Player ko kaise pata chalta hai kaunsi quality chunni hai?

Player saare renditions waala manifest download karta hai, phir har segment ke liye estimated bandwidth aur current buffer se bitrate chunta hai (ABR algorithms jaise throughput-based ya buffer-based/BOLA). Tez start ke liye low se shuru karta hai aur buffer badhne pe upar chadhta hai.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — Transcoding fleet

Roz 400K uploads, average length 8 minute. Saare renditions encode karne mein video ke har minute pe ~2 CPU-minutes lagte hain. 70% utilisation pe steady state mein 32-core ki kitni machines chahiye?

Solution. Video minutes/din = 3.2M. CPU-minutes = 6.4M/din ÷ 1,440 = average ~4,444 cores busy. 32 cores ke 70% pe (22.4 usable) → average ~200 machines; peaks ko zyada chahiye (ya burst sokhne waali queue). Spot/preemptible instances achhe fit hain kyunki tasks retryable hain.

Practice 2 — CDN vs origin split

Roz 15 PB egress. 80% views top 10% videos ko jaate hain. CDN $0.02/GB leta hai, origin se serve karna $0.008/GB par sirf long tail ke liye chalta hai. Sab CDN se serve karne ke muqable roz kitni bachat?

Solution. Sab CDN: 15M GB × $0.02 = $300K/din. Split: 12 PB CDN se = $240K; 3 PB origin se = $24K → $264K/din. Bachat ≈ $36K/din (~$13M/saal).

Practice 3 — Segment ka hisaab

10-minute video, 6 renditions, 4-second segments. Kitni segment files? Agar player har segment pe naya bitrate chune, toh quality kitni baar badal sakti hai?

Solution. 600 s / 4 s = 150 segments × 6 = 900 files (+ 7 playlists). Quality har 4 second badal sakti hai.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• Storage aur CDN egress estimate kar sakta hoon aur samjha sakta hoon ki CDN cost kyun haavi hai.
  • Upload flow (pre-signed URL, original storage, pipeline, completion queue, metadata) aur streaming flow bana sakta hoon.
  • Containers vs codecs, aur hum kai renditions mein transcode kyun karte hain — samjha sakta hoon.
  • Segments aur manifests ke saath HLS/DASH aur adaptive bitrate samjha sakta hoon.
  • Transcoding DAG aur planner → orchestrator → dispatch queues → worker pools roles describe kar sakta hoon.
  • Speed, security aur cost optimisations aur errors handle karna pata hai.

Aage: 15 · Google Drive

docs.title: 15 · Google Drive Design karo
docs.text:
⏱ 45 min read 🔥 Sync, consistency aur storage efficiency test karta hai Book: Chapter 15

TL;DR

  • Files blocks mein toot-ti hain (jaise 4 MB), har ek ki pehchaan uska content hash. Sirf badle hue blocks upload/download → delta sync; identical blocks ek hi baar store → dedup.
  • Bytes block servers ke through object storage (S3) mein; baaki sab — users, devices, files, versions, block lists — strongly consistent metadata DB (relational, ACID) mein.
  • File badalne pe notification service (long polling) user ke baaki devices ko batati hai; woh nayi block list laate hain aur sirf missing blocks download karte hain. Offline devices offline backup queue / change log se catch up karte hain.
  • Conflicts: jo version pehle commit hua woh jeetta hai; doosra "conflicted copy" ban jaata hai jo user resolve karta hai.
  • Cost control: dedup, limited version history (aur purane versions patle karna), aur kam access hone waale data ke liye cold storage.

docs.title: Intuition: register waali saanjhi almaari
docs.text:
Socho ek ghar ki almaari jisme sab documents rakhte hain, aur aage ek register hai jo har document, uske pages, aur aakhri baar kisne badla, list karta hai. 100-page file mein sirf page 37 badla toh poori file nahi badalte — page 37 badlo aur register update karo. Do log ek saath same page edit karein, toh jo register mein pehle likhe woh jeetta hai; doosre ka version "copy 2" ki tarah rakh liya jaata hai. Doosre shehron mein rehne waale family members ko phone aata hai: "register update hua" — aur woh sirf naya page mangwaate hain.

Pages = blocks. Register = metadata DB. Phone call = notification service.

docs.title: Step 1 · Scope
docs.text:
Clarifying baatcheet

Tum: Personal storage hai, team storage, ya dono? — Interviewer: Pehle personal, folder sharing ke saath. Tum: "Sync" ka matlab kya — har device hamesha cloud ka mirror? — I: Haan, desktop clients local mirror rakhte hain; phones zaroorat pe laate hain. Tum: Files kitni badi ho sakti hain? — I: 5 GB tak. Tum: Free quota? — I: Har user 10 GB. Tum: Kitne users? — I: 40M registered, roz 8M active. Tum: Purane versions rakhne hain? — I: Haan, users purane versions restore kar sakein. Tum: Security expectations? — I: Transit mein aur at rest encrypted.

Scope se bahar (sirf mention): real-time collaborative editing (woh Google Docs hai — operational transforms/CRDTs, alag problem).

Non-functional: reliability (data kabhi na khoye — #1 requirement), tez sync, kam bandwidth (mobile data mehenga hai), scalability, high availability.

docs.title: Estimates
docs.text: Cheez Value Allocated storage 40M × 10 GB = 400 PB allocated (asli use shayad 30–40% → ~140 PB) Uploads 8M DAU × 3 files/din = 24M/din → ~280/s, peak ~600/s Average file ~1 MB → dedup se pehle roz ~24 TB naya data Metadata reads sync checks, folders list karna: uploads ka ~10× → ~3K/s

docs.title: Simple shuruaat: ek server
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|"upload / download / revisions"| WS["Web server<br/>(Apache)"] --> DB[(MySQL metadata)]
    WS --> FS[("Local disk<br/>/drive/{namespace}/…")]

APIs:

POST /files/upload?uploadType=resumable      # resumable upload shuru → upload session URL milta hai
PUT  <session URL>  (bytes, Content-Range)   # data bhejo; failures ke baad resume
GET  /files/download?path=/docs/resume.pdf
GET  /files/list_revisions?path=/docs/resume.pdf&limit=20
  • Chhoti files ke liye simple upload; badi files ke liye resumable upload — toota connection jhel lo bina dobara shuru kiye.
  • Saare endpoints HTTPS pe auth (OAuth tokens) maangte hain.

Disk bharne tak chalta hai. Ab scale karo.

docs.title: Scale out
docs.text:
• Storage → files ko object storage (S3) pe le jao: region ke andar replicated; cross-region replication on karo taaki regional disaster mein data na khoye.
  • Load balancer + kai stateless web/API servers.
  • Metadata DB → alag, replicated (aur baad mein sharded) relational DB.
  • Block servers storage pe upload se pehle files ko blocks mein todte hain.

docs.title: Poora design
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    U["Clients<br/>desktop · mobile · web"] -->|"API: metadata"| LB{{Load balancer}} --> API[API servers]
    U -->|"blocks"| BS["Block servers<br/>split · compress · encrypt"]
    BS --> S3[(Cloud storage<br/>S3)]
    S3 -.->|"kam use"| COLD[(Cold storage)]
    API --> MC[(Metadata cache)] --> MDB[(Metadata DB<br/>strongly consistent)]
    API --> NS["Notification service<br/>(long polling)"]
    NS <-->|"long poll"| U
    API --> OQ[["Offline backup queue"]]
Component Role Block servers Files ko blocks mein todo, compress, encrypt, aur cloud storage pe upload; download pe wapas jodo. Har block ki ID = uske content ka hash. Cloud storage Blocks rakhta hai (immutable objects). Cold storage Inactive files ke liye sasta tier (jaise S3 Glacier). API servers Bytes ke alawa sab: auth, profiles, file metadata, sharing, versions. Metadata DB Users, devices, files, versions, block lists, sharing. Strong consistency. Metadata cache Tez reads ke liye hot metadata. Notification service Clients ko "kuch badla" publish karti hai (long polling). Offline backup queue Offline devices ke liye changes rakhti hai, taaki baad mein sync kar sakein.

docs.title: Block servers: delta sync aur compression
docs.text:
Ek paragraph badalne pe poori 2 GB file upload karna bandwidth ki barbaadi hai. Toh:

  1. File ko blocks mein todo (Dropbox famously max 4 MB use karta tha).
  2. Har block hash karo (SHA-256) → block ID.
  3. Server se poochho kaunsi block IDs uske paas pehle se hain; sirf missing upload karo (delta sync).
  4. Har block ko bhejne se pehle compress (text ke liye gzip/zstd; images/video pehle se compressed) aur encrypt karo.
flowchart LR
    F["resume.pdf (v2)"] --> SPLIT["blocks mein todo<br/>b1 b2 b3 b4"]
    SPLIT --> H["har block hash"]
    H --> CMP{"server ke paas<br/>block hai?"}
    CMP -->|"b1, b2, b4: haan"| SKIP[skip]
    CMP -->|"b3: nahi (badla)"| UP["compress → encrypt → b3 upload"]

Fixed vs content-defined chunking. Fixed-size blocks mein shuruaat mein ek byte daalne se har block boundary khisak jaati hai → har block ka hash badal jaata hai. Content-defined chunking (rolling hash, jaise Rabin fingerprints) blocks wahan kaat-ta hai jahan content mein khaas patterns hain, toh insertion sirf apne aas-paas ka block badalta hai.

/** SHA-256 block IDs ke saath fixed-size chunking (content-defined chunking split rule badal dega). */
static List<String> blockIds(Path file, int blockSize) throws Exception {
    List<String> ids = new ArrayList<>();
    MessageDigest sha = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
    try (InputStream in = Files.newInputStream(file)) {
        byte[] buf = new byte[blockSize];
        int n;
        while ((n = in.readNBytes(buf, 0, blockSize)) > 0) {
            ids.add(HexFormat.of().formatHex(sha.digest(Arrays.copyOf(buf, n))));
        }
    }
    return ids;   // file ka version = block IDs ki yeh ordered list
}

docs.title: Metadata ke liye strong consistency kyun
docs.text:
Agar do devices same file ki block list ke alag versions dekhein, toh woh alag content dikhayenge — ya badtar, ek-doosre ko overwrite kar denge. Metadata strongly consistent hona chahiye (commit ke baad har read commit dekhe), chahe thodi availability ki keemat lage.

  • ACID transactions waala relational DB use karo — naya version commit karna (version row + block list insert + "latest" pointer update) ek transaction hai.
  • Caches consistent rakhne padte hain: cache ke replicas master se agree karein; har metadata write pe cache invalidate karo.
  • Kai NoSQL stores default mein eventual consistency dete hain → extra dhyaan chahiye. Bytes (blocks) ko iski zaroorat nahi — woh immutable aur content-addressed hain, kabhi "inconsistent" ho hi nahi sakte.

docs.title: Metadata schema
docs.text:
erDiagram
    USER ||--o{ DEVICE : has
    USER ||--o{ NAMESPACE : owns
    NAMESPACE ||--o{ FILE : contains
    FILE ||--o{ FILE_VERSION : has
    FILE_VERSION ||--o{ VERSION_BLOCK : "ordered list of"
    BLOCK ||--o{ VERSION_BLOCK : "used by"
    USER {
        bigint user_id PK
        string email
        bigint quota_used
    }
    DEVICE {
        uuid device_id PK
        bigint user_id FK
        bigint last_synced_change
        timestamp last_seen
    }
    NAMESPACE {
        bigint namespace_id PK
        bigint owner_id FK
    }
    FILE {
        bigint file_id PK
        bigint namespace_id FK
        string path
        int latest_version
        bool is_deleted
        string checksum
    }
    FILE_VERSION {
        bigint file_id FK
        int version_no
        uuid device_id
        timestamp created_at
    }
    BLOCK {
        string block_hash PK
        int size
        int ref_count
    }
    VERSION_BLOCK {
        bigint file_id FK
        int version_no FK
        int position
        string block_hash FK
    }
  • Namespace = user ka root folder (ya shared folder).
  • File versions immutable rows hain — kabhi update nahi, sirf append → "pichla version restore" ke liye poori history.
  • Version block hashes ki ordered list hai. Dedup aur garbage collection ke liye blocks ka ref_count hai.

docs.title: Upload flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C1 as Client 1 (laptop)
    participant API as API servers
    participant MDB as Metadata DB
    participant BS as Block servers
    participant S3 as Cloud storage
    participant NS as Notification service
    participant C2 as Client 2 (phone)
    par metadata
        C1->>API: report.xlsx ka naya version (block list)
        API->>MDB: status = uploading, pending version record
        API->>NS: notify: report.xlsx upload ho raha hai
        NS->>C2: change event
    and bytes
        C1->>BS: sirf missing blocks
        BS->>S3: blocks store (compressed, encrypted)
        S3-->>API: upload-complete callback
        API->>MDB: version commit, status = uploaded
        API->>NS: notify: report.xlsx update hua
        NS->>C2: change event
    end

Do requests parallel mein: (1) file metadata jodo (status pending/uploading), aur (2) blocks upload karo. Storage saare blocks confirm kare toh version commit hota hai (status uploaded) aur baaki devices ko notify kiya jaata hai.

docs.title: Download / sync flow
docs.text:
Device ko kaise pata chale ki kuch badla?

  • Online: notification service batati hai.
  • Offline: changes jama hote rehte hain (offline backup queue / change log mein); reconnect pe device poochta hai "change #N ke baad kya badla?" (last_synced_change).
sequenceDiagram
    participant NS as Notification service
    participant C2 as Client 2
    participant API as API servers
    participant MDB as Metadata DB
    participant BS as Block servers
    participant S3 as Cloud storage
    NS->>C2: report.xlsx badla
    C2->>API: #N ke baad ke changes do
    API->>MDB: naya version + block list laao
    MDB-->>API: blocks [b1,b2,b7,b4]
    API-->>C2: block list
    C2->>C2: local blocks se compare → b7 chahiye
    C2->>BS: b7 download
    BS->>S3: b7 lao
    S3-->>BS: b7
    BS-->>C2: b7 (decrypt, decompress)
    C2->>C2: file jodo, last_synced_change update

docs.title: Notification service: long polling kyun?
docs.text:
Long polling WebSocket Kis direction ki zaroorat Sirf server → client, kabhi-kabhi Bi-directional, baar-baar Drive ke liye fit ✅ changes kabhi-kabhi bursts mein; client phir normal APIs call karta hai Zaroorat se zyada Chat ke liye fit (Ch. 12) Kamzor ✅

Har client ek long-poll connection rakhta hai; change aaye (ya poll time out ho) toh server respond karta hai; client metadata changes laata hai aur reconnect karta hai. Connections pakadna sasta hai par bahut saare — har cluster pe lakhon. Notification server mare toh clients doosre se reconnect karte hain (data nahi kho sakte — woh change log le aayenge).

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
Do devices sync se pehle same file edit karte hain. Jo version pehle commit hua woh jeetta hai; doosra conflicted copy ki tarah save hota hai (report (Asha's laptop's conflicted copy 2026-11-17).xlsx) aur user haath se merge karta hai. (Automatic merging sirf structured formats ke liye chalta hai — woh collaborative editing hai, scope se bahar.)

"Pehla jeetta hai" optimistic concurrency se implement karo: commit bolta hai "version 7 pe based naya version"; agar latest ab 7 nahi, toh commit conflict ki tarah reject.

docs.title: Storage space bachana
docs.text:
Storage hamesha badhta rehta hai jab tak uske khilaaf design na karo. Chaar levers, typical deployment mein sabse badi jeet se chhoti tak:

  1. Content-addressed blocks dedup muft mein dete hain. Same hash → same object; bas ref_count badhao. Per-account dedup safe hai; users ke across global dedup zyada bachata hai par yeh bata sakta hai ki kisi aur user ke paas pehle se file hai, toh dhyaan se lagao.
  2. Versions saste hain par muft nahi. Naya version sirf badle blocks jodta hai, toh history ka kharcha kam — par har kuch second auto-save karne waala app phir bhi hazaaron versions bana sakta hai. Umar ke saath history patli karo (recent versions ghane, purane virle) aur har plan ki retention cap karo.
  3. Tiering. Jo data mahino se kisi ne nahi khola woh kahin saste archive tier pe jaata hai; restore slow hota hai, jo purani files ke liye users shaayad hi notice karte hain.
  4. Garbage collection. Versions expire ya files delete hone pe jin blocks ka ref_count zero ho jaaye woh hata do — grace period ke baad, bugs ya restores ke case mein.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
Failures ko kya daav pe hai se sort karo:

Kya data kho sakta hai? Sabse important yahi hai.

  • Blocks region ke andar replicate hone waale object storage mein likhe jaate hain, aur hum doosre region mein bhi replicate karte hain; version tabhi commit hota hai jab uske saare blocks durably store ho jaayein — toh upload ke beech crash ek uncommitted version chhodta hai, kabhi corrupt file nahi.
  • Metadata DB synchronous replicas aur automatic leader failover ke saath chalta hai; regular backups aur point-in-time recovery galat writes (bugs, galti se mass deletes) se bachate hain.

Kya sync atak sakta hai?

  • Notification server mare toh uske clients ke long polls toot-te hain; woh kahin aur reconnect karke poochte hain "mere aakhri sync ke baad kya badla?" — change log chhoote notifications ko harmless bana deta hai.
  • Offline devices ke change events replicated queues/logs mein rehte hain, toh broker failure sync ko late karta hai par kuch nahi khota.

Kya requests fail ho sakti hain?

  • API servers aur block servers redundant load balancers ke peeche stateless hain; adhoora block job doosra server bas retry kar leta hai (block uploads idempotent hain — same hash, same object).
  • Metadata cache replicated hai; ek node khone ka matlab bas replace hone tak zyada DB reads.

docs.title: Step 4 · Wrap-up — aur directions
docs.text:
• Chunking kahan honi chahiye? Humne splitting/compression/encryption block servers mein rakha taaki logic ek trusted jagah rahe. Alternative — clients signed URLs se seedha object storage pe blocks upload karein — ek hop aur server cost hatata hai, par har client platform (Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, web) ko same chunking aur crypto sahi implement karna padega, aur buggy ya tampered client kharab data upload kar sakta hai. Kai asli systems hybrid karte hain: clients chunk aur hash karte hain, servers verify.
  • Selective sync / on-demand files. Desktop clients placeholders dikhate hain aur content sirf khulne pe download karte hain — zaroori jab users ka cloud data laptop disk se zyada ho jaaye.
  • Sharing aur permissions. Har namespace/file ke ACLs, expire hone waale share links, aur har metadata aur block request pe permission checks.
  • Search. File names (aur optionally contents) ko asynchronously search service mein index karo, permissions ka dhyaan rakhte hue.
  • Presence. Agar doosre features ko "kaun online hai" chahiye, toh use notification service se nikaal ke apni service banao.

docs.title: Interviewer follow-ups
docs.text:
User 1 GB file mein 1 byte badalta hai. Kya upload hota hai?

4 MB fixed blocks ke saath, us byte waala block badalta hai → ~4 MB (compressed) upload, 1 GB nahi. Agar bytes insert hue (modify nahi), toh fixed chunking har baad waale block ko khiska degi; content-defined chunking change ko local rakhti hai, toh ab bhi sirf ek-do blocks upload hote hain.

Metadata ke liye Dynamo jaisi eventual consistency kyun nahi?

Kyunki diverge hua metadata matlab devices is baat pe asehmat hain ki file kin blocks se bani hai — users alag content dekhenge ya chupchaap ek-doosre ke changes overwrite karenge. Sync correctness ko "latest version" ka ek, linearizable view aur atomic commits chahiye; metadata ke liye hum availability/latency ki keemat maante hain jabki bhaari, immutable blocks highly available store mein rehte hain.

Upload resumable kaise banaoge?

Client pehle upload register karta hai (session ID aur un blocks ki list milti hai jo server ko abhi chahiye). Har block alag upload aur acknowledge hota hai. Crash ya disconnect ke baad client session se poochta hai kaunse blocks abhi missing hain aur sirf wahi bhejta hai. Version tabhi commit hota hai jab saare blocks confirm ho jaayein.

Ek hafte se offline phone efficiently kaise catch up karega?

Woh last_synced_change = N bhejta hai; server N ke baad ki change log entries return karta hai (file IDs aur unke latest versions — har beech ka version nahi). Phone sirf un files ki block lists aur sirf woh blocks download karta hai jo uske paas nahi. Bade backlog ke liye pehle woh folders sync kar sakta hai jo user sach mein kholta hai (selective sync).

Folder ko doosre user ke saath share karna kaise implement karoge?

Shared folders ACL (owner, editors, viewers) waale namespaces hain. Recipient ka device us namespace ke notifications subscribe karta hai; metadata queries mein woh saare namespaces shaamil hote hain jinhe user access kar sakta hai. Permission checks API servers aur block servers (signed, scoped block URLs) mein har access pe hote hain.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — Delta sync bandwidth

Ek designer 200 MB ki PSD din mein 30 baar save karta hai; har save file ka ~5% badalta hai, ~6 blocks (4 MB) mein bikhra hua. Full-file upload vs block-level delta sync mein roz kitna upload hota hai?

Solution. Full: 30 × 200 MB = 6 GB/din. Delta: 30 × 6 × 4 MB = 720 MB/din (compression se pehle ≈ 8× kam).

Practice 2 — Dedup ki bachat

Ek company ke 10,000 employees hain; har ek ki Drive mein same 300 MB ka onboarding folder hai. Per-company dedup ke saath aur bina storage?

Solution. Bina: 10,000 × 300 MB = 3 TB. Dedup ke saath: 300 MB (+ metadata aur ref counts). Isliye workplaces mein block-level, content-addressed storage itna effective hai.

Practice 3 — Version thinning

Ek file roz 8 ghante har 30 second auto-save hoti hai. Aisi retention policy design karo jo pichla ghanta minute-by-minute, pichla hafta hourly, aur 30 din tak purani history daily rakhe. Max kitne versions rakhe jaayenge?

Solution. Pichla ghanta: 60; pichla hafta (pichle ghante ke alawa): ~7 × 24 = 168; din 8–30: 23 → 960/din × 30 = 28,800 ki jagah ~251 versions.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• Requirements bata sakta hoon aur storage aur upload QPS estimate kar sakta hoon.
  • Single-server design ko poore architecture mein badal ke har component samjha sakta hoon.
  • Block splitting, hashing, delta sync, compression, encryption — aur content-defined chunking samjha sakta hoon.
  • Metadata ke liye strong consistency justify kar sakta hoon aur metadata schema design kar sakta hoon.
  • Offline devices samet upload aur download/sync flows samjha sakta hoon.
  • Notifications ke liye long polling, conflict handling, storage savings aur failure handling samjha sakta hoon.

Aage: 16 · Revision Cheat Sheet

docs.title: 01 · Zero se Millions Users tak Scale
docs.text:
⏱ 45 min read 🔥 Baaki har chapter ki neev Book: Chapter 1

TL;DR

  • Shuruaat ek server se karo, phir jo hissa bottleneck bane usse alag karte jao: database → web tier → cache → static files → sessions → data centers → async kaam → phir se database.
  • Scale out karo, up nahi: load balancer ke peeche zyada machines lagao aur web tier ko stateless rakho taaki koi bhi server koi bhi request handle kar sake.
  • Database ko replicate karo (writes ke liye ek leader, reads ke liye kai followers), uske aage cache lagao, aur static files CDN pe daalo.
  • Slow kaam ko message queue se decouple karo, aur availability ke liye multiple data centers + geo-routing use karo.
  • Jab ek database data sambhal na paaye, toh shard karo — shard key chunna sabse bada decision hai, aur hotspots/resharding/joins uski keemat hain.

docs.title: Intuition: ek dhaba jo chain ban jaata hai
docs.text:
Socho highway pe ek dhaba hai jo ek hi banda chalata hai. Wahi order leta hai, wahi khana banata hai, wahi serve karta hai, wahi paisa leta hai. Yeh hai single server. Lunch rush tak sab theek chalta hai.

  • Pehle woh ek alag cook rakhta hai, taaki counter waala sirf order le → database ko web server se alag karna.
  • Phir zyada counters khulte hain, aur darwaze pe ek banda khada hai jo bolta hai "counter 3 pe jao" → load balancer + zyada web servers.
  • Cook recipe book ek baar likhta hai aur helpers ko copies de deta hai, jo sirf padh sakte hain → database replication.
  • Sabse popular dishes pehle se bana ke garam rakhi jaati hain → cache.
  • Cold drinks main kitchen ki jagah har colony ke paas stall se bikti hain → CDN.
  • Order slips ek rail pe lagti hain aur cooks free hote hi utha lete hain → message queue.
  • Aakhir mein alag-alag shehron mein branches khulti hain → multiple data centers, aur menu specialised kitchens mein bant jaata hai → sharding.

Is chapter ki har technique bas yahi kahani hai, computers ke saath.

docs.title: Stage 0 · Ek single server
docs.text:
Sab kuch — web app, database, cache — ek hi machine pe. Ek request trace karte hain, kyunki aage ka har design isi flow ka variation hai.

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User (browser / app)
    participant D as DNS
    participant S as Web server
    U->>D: shop.example.in kahan hai?
    D-->>U: 203.0.113.42
    U->>S: GET /products/42 (HTTP)
    S->>S: business logic chalao, DB padho
    S-->>U: 200 OK + JSON / HTML
  1. User domain type karta hai. DNS (aam taur pe Route 53 ya Cloudflare jaisi paid third-party service) usse IP address mein badalta hai.
  2. Client us IP pe seedha HTTP request bhejta hai.
  3. Server HTML (browser ke liye) ya JSON (mobile apps aur SPAs ke liye) wapas bhejta hai.

Traffic do tarah ke clients se aata hai: web apps (Java/Python/Go mein server-side code + browser mein HTML/JS) aur mobile apps (HTTP pe baat karte hain, mostly JSON — jaise GET /products/42 → {"id":42,"name":"Kurta","price":899}).

Yeh zyada din kyun nahi chalega

Ek machine = ek single point of failure (SPOF). Woh reboot hui toh product band. Aur CPU, RAM, disk web app aur database dono share karte hain, toh dono aapas mein ladte hain.

docs.title: Stage 1 · Database alag karo
docs.text:
Database ko apni alag machine pe le jao. Ab web tier (requests handle karta hai) aur data tier (data store karta hai) alag-alag scale ho sakte hain — jaldi hi tumhe 20 web servers chahiye honge, par primary database shayad ek hi.

flowchart LR
    U[Users] --> W[Web server]
    W -->|read / write| DB[(Database)]

docs.title: Kaunsa database? SQL vs NoSQL
docs.text:
Yeh decision har design mein aayega, toh achhe se samajh lete hain.

Relational (SQL) Non-relational (NoSQL) Examples MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle Cassandra, DynamoDB, MongoDB, HBase, Redis, Neo4j Data model Tables, rows, fixed schema Key-value, document, wide-column, graph Joins Haan, powerful SQL Usually nahi (denormalise karte hain) Transactions Rows/tables ke across full ACID Aksar ek key / ek partition tak limited Writes scale karna Ek primary ke aage mushkil (sharding chahiye) Shuru se kai nodes pe partition hone ke liye bane hain Best for Paisa, orders, inventory — jahan relations aur integrity rules hon Bahut bada volume, simple access patterns, flexible schema, low latency

Default SQL rakho. Dashakon ki tooling aur correctness guarantees hain. NoSQL tab lo jab inme se kuch sach ho:

  • Bahut bade scale pe simple lookups ke liye bahut low latency chahiye (session store, feature flags).
  • Data unstructured / semi-structured hai ya schema baar-baar badalta hai (product catalog jahan har product ke attributes alag hain).
  • Tum mostly key se blobs serialize/deserialize kar rahe ho (JSON documents).
  • Massive data store karna hai (billions of rows, petabytes) aur joins se zyada write throughput important hai.

NoSQL ki chaar families, ek-ek line mein:

Family Mental model Example use Key-value Ek giant distributed HashMap<String, byte[]> Sessions, carts, caches (Redis, DynamoDB) Document Key → JSON document jiske andar query kar sakte ho User profiles, catalogs (MongoDB) Wide-column Row key → columns ka sorted map, heavy writes ke liye bana Chat messages, time series (Cassandra, HBase) Graph Nodes + edges, fast traversal Social graph, recommendations (Neo4j)

Interview mein

"NoSQL kyunki woh scale karta hai" mat bolo. Batao access pattern kya hai aur woh store usme kyun fit hota hai: "Messages lagatar likhe jaate hain aur (channel, time range) se padhe jaate hain, isliye Cassandra jaisa wide-column store — channel_id se partitioned aur message_id se clustered — perfect fit hai."

docs.title: Stage 2 · Vertical vs horizontal scaling
docs.text:
Vertical ("scale up") Horizontal ("scale out") Kya Badi machine: zyada CPU, RAM, tez disk Zyada machines jo load baant lein Fayde Ekdum simple, code change nahi, distributed-systems ki problems nahi Practically unlimited, ek machine fail ho toh bhi chalta rahe Nuksaan Hard ceiling; cost tezi se badhti hai; phir bhi ek SPOF; upgrade mein downtime Load balancing, stateless servers, data partitioning chahiye Kab Traffic kam/moderate ho, ya shuru mein database ke liye Bada scale, high availability chahiye

Vertical scaling "bura" nahi hai — database ke liye aksar pehla sahi step yahi hota hai (ek bada Postgres box kaafi door tak le jaata hai). Par web tier ke liye jaldi se horizontal scaling chahiye, aur uske liye load balancer.

docs.title: Stage 3 · Load balancer
docs.text:
Load balancer (LB) web servers ke pool ke aage baithta hai aur requests unme baant-ta hai.

flowchart LR
    U[Users] -->|public IP| LB{{Load balancer}}
    LB -->|private IP| W1[Web server 1]
    LB -->|private IP| W2[Web server 2]
    W1 --> DB[(Database)]
    W2 --> DB
  • Users ko sirf LB ka public IP pata hai. Servers private IPs pe hain (network ke andar reachable, internet se nahi) — security better.
  • Server 1 mar gaya? LB ke health checks pakad lete hain aur sab traffic server 2 pe bhej dete hain → failover.
  • Traffic badha? Pool mein server 3, 4, 5 daal do → LB automatically unhe use karna shuru kar deta hai.

docs.title: LB server kaise chunta hai?
docs.text: Algorithm Kaise Kiske liye achha Round robin 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3… Same servers, similar requests Weighted round robin Bade servers ko zyada turns Mixed hardware Least connections Jiske paas sabse kam active connections Long-lived ya uneven requests (WebSockets, uploads) Least response time Sabse tez jawab dene waala healthy server Latency-sensitive APIs IP hash / consistent hashing hash(client IP ya key) → server Stickiness, cache locality

docs.title: L4 vs L7 load balancing
docs.text:
• Layer 4 (transport): sirf IP + port dekh ke route karta hai, HTTP request kabhi nahi padhta. Bahut tez, kisi bhi protocol ke saath chale. Example: AWS NLB.
  • Layer 7 (application): HTTP request padhta hai — path, headers, cookies — toh /api/* ko API servers pe aur /static/* ko kahin aur bhej sakta hai, TLS terminate kar sakta hai, auth aur rate limiting kar sakta hai. Example: NGINX, Envoy, AWS ALB.

\"Toh kya load balancer khud single point of failure nahi hai?\"

Haan, agar ek hi ho. Asli setups mein LBs pairs mein chalte hain (active-passive with floating/virtual IP, ya active-active), aur DNS kai LB IPs de sakta hai. Cloud ke managed LBs pehle se availability zones ke across replicated hote hain.

docs.title: Stage 4 · Database replication
docs.text:
Web tier ab failures jhel leta hai. Database nahi. Replication data ki copies kai servers pe rakhta hai.

Classic setup hai leader–follower (book purane master–slave words use karti hai):

  • Leader (primary) saare writes leta hai — INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.
  • Followers (replicas) ko har change ki copy milti hai aur woh reads serve karte hain.
  • Zyada tar apps likhne se kahin zyada padhte hain (aksar 10:1 se 100:1), toh ek leader, kai followers.
flowchart TB
    W[Web servers] -->|writes| L[(Leader DB)]
    W -->|reads| F1[(Follower 1)]
    W -->|reads| F2[(Follower 2)]
    W -->|reads| F3[(Follower 3)]
    L -. replication log .-> F1
    L -. replication log .-> F2
    L -. replication log .-> F3

Kya milta hai

  • Performance — reads kai machines pe bant jaate hain aur parallel chalte hain.
  • Reliability — disk fail ho, ya poora data center jal jaaye, data bacha rahta hai agar replicas kahin aur hain.
  • Availability — ek DB machine down ho toh baaki jawab dete rahte hain.

Kuch fail ho toh kya hota hai

  • Follower mar gaya → reads baaki followers pe (ya kuch der leader pe); naya follower snapshot + log se banta hai.
  • Leader mar gaya → ek follower ko promote karke leader banate hain (failover). Mushkil hissa: woh follower thoda peeche ho sakta hai, toh last kuch writes gayab ho sakte hain. Production systems consensus (jaise etcd mein Raft, MySQL ke liye Orchestrator) aur careful recovery use karte hain yeh decide karne ke liye ki sabse fresh kaun hai.

docs.title: Thoda gehraai mein: sync vs async replication aur lag
docs.text:
Mode Leader kiska wait karta hai… Fayda Nuksaan Synchronous Follower confirm kare, tab client ko "OK" Follower kabhi peeche nahi Ek slow follower har write slow kar deta hai Asynchronous Kisi ka nahi — turant reply Tez writes Replication lag: followers seconds peeche ho sakte hain Semi-sync Kam se kam ek follower Achha compromise Writes thode slow

Replication lag asli bugs banata hai. Classic example — read-your-own-writes:

Riya apni profile photo update karti hai (write → leader). Page reload hota hai aur ek follower se padhta hai jisko change abhi mila hi nahi. Usse purani photo dikhti hai aur woh sochti hai upload fail ho gaya.

Fixes: user ke apne data ko write ke baad thodi der tak leader se padho; ya replication position track karo aur sirf un followers se padho jo catch-up kar chuke hain; ya user ke hisaab se route karo taaki user ek hi replica pe tike.

Leader–follower se aage

Multi-leader (kai DCs writes lete hain, phir sync karte hain) aur leaderless (Dynamo-style, koi bhi node write le sakta hai, quorum decide karta hai) bhi hote hain. Yeh simplicity deke availability lete hain, aur write conflicts laate hain. Chapter 6 (Key-Value Store) leaderless replication mein gehraai se jaata hai.

docs.title: Stage 5 · Cache
docs.text:
Har page load database ko kai baar hit karta hai. Cache mehnge ya baar-baar hone waale reads ke results ko memory mein rakhta hai, jo disk-wale database se lagbhag 100–1000× tez hai.

flowchart LR
    W[Web server] -->|1. key lao| C[(Cache<br/>Redis / Memcached)]
    C -->|2a. hit: return| W
    W -->|2b. miss: query| DB[(Database)]
    DB -->|3. rows| W
    W -->|4. key set karo, TTL| C

Upar waala flow — pehle cache check karo, miss pe DB padho aur cache bhar do — sabse common pattern hai. Book ise read-through cache kehti hai; bahut engineers isi flow ko cache-aside kehte hain (application khud cache bharti hai). Java mein:

public User getUser(long id) {
    String key = "user:" + id;
    User cached = cache.get(key);              // 1. pehle cache try karo
    if (cached != null) return cached;         // 2a. hit

    User fromDb = userRepository.findById(id); // 2b. miss → database
    if (fromDb != null) {
        cache.set(key, fromDb, Duration.ofMinutes(10)); // 3. TTL ke saath bhar do
    }
    return fromDb;
}

public void updateUser(User u) {
    userRepository.save(u);         // pehle source of truth mein likho
    cache.delete("user:" + u.id()); // phir cached copy delete karo (update nahi)
}

docs.title: Caching strategies — poora menu
docs.text: Strategy Read path Write path Kab use karein Cache-aside (lazy loading) App cache check kare, miss pe DB se laaye aur bhar de App DB mein likhe, cache key delete kare Read-heavy apps ka default Read-through Cache library khud miss pe DB se load kare — Loading logic cache layer mein chahiye Write-through — Cache aur DB dono mein synchronously likho Write ke turant baad data cache mein chahiye Write-behind (write-back) — Abhi cache mein likho, baad mein batch mein DB mein flush Bahut write-heavy, thoda loss chalega (counters, likes) Write-around — Sirf DB mein likho; agle read pe cache bharega Data ek baar likha, kam dobara padha jaata hai

docs.title: Cache lagane se pehle kya sochna hai
docs.text:
1. Kab cache karein. Jo data zyada padha, kam badla jaata hai. Cache ko kabhi akeli copy mat samjho — volatile memory mein hai, restart hua toh sab gaya.
  2. Expiration (TTL). Iske bina stale data hamesha pada rahega aur memory bhar jaayegi. Bahut chhota → DB ko baar-baar reload se pareshan karoge; bahut lamba → users ko purana data dikhega. Minutes se hours typical hai; har data type ke liye tune karo.
  3. Consistency. DB write aur cache update ek transaction nahi hain, toh drift ho sakta hai (khaaskar regions ke across). Write pe key delete karna (upar jaisa) update karne se safe hai, kyunki do concurrent updates galat value nahi chhod sakte. Facebook ka Scaling Memcache paper isi mushkil ka classic reference hai.
  4. Failure. Ek cache server = SPOF. Kai chalao (zones / DCs ke across) aur memory over-provision karo taaki node loss ya growth spike pe mass eviction na ho.
  5. Eviction policy. Memory full hui toh kuch toh hatega:
    • LRU (least recently used) — usual default.
    • LFU (least frequently used) — jab popularity stable ho tab better.
    • FIFO — sabse simple, rarely best.

Cache stampede (thundering herd)

Ek hot key (jaise home-page feed) expire hui. 10,000 requests ek saath miss hui aur sab ek saath database pe gir padi — DB gir gaya. Fixes: sirf ek request ko key rebuild karne do (lock ya single-flight), jab tak ek worker refresh kare tab tak stale value serve karo, aur TTLs mein random jitter daalo taaki saari keys same second pe expire na hon.

docs.title: Stage 6 · Content Delivery Network (CDN)
docs.text:
Images, videos, CSS aur JS static hain — har user ke liye same bytes. Inhe web servers se serve karna unka CPU aur bandwidth barbaad karta hai aur door ke users ke liye slow hai. CDN duniya bhar mein phaile servers ka network hai (edge locations) jo static content users ke paas cache karta hai.

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as User A (Mumbai)
    participant E as CDN edge (Mumbai)
    participant O as Origin (S3 / web server)
    participant B as User B (Pune)
    A->>E: GET cdn.example.in/logo.png
    E->>O: miss → logo.png laao
    O-->>E: logo.png + Cache-Control TTL
    E-->>A: logo.png (ab edge pe cached)
    B->>E: GET cdn.example.in/logo.png
    E-->>B: hit → Mumbai se hi serve, origin ko pata bhi nahi
  • URL CDN ke domain ki taraf point karta hai (jaise cdn.example.in/..., jo CDN provider pe mapped hai).
  • Miss pe edge origin (tumhara server ya S3) se laata hai, origin ke bataye TTL tak cache karta hai, aur return karta hai.
  • Us region ki har agli request TTL khatam hone tak hit hai.

Pull vs push CDN. Pull (upar waala) pehli request pe lazily laata hai — easy, zyada tar sites ke liye achha. Push matlab tum content pehle se CDN pe upload karte ho — badi files ke liye kaam ka jo popular hone waali hain (nayi movie release).

Kya sochna hai

  • Cost — per GB transfer ka paisa lagta hai. Kam access hone waali files CDN pe mat daalo.
  • Expiry — time-sensitive content ko sensible TTL chahiye.
  • CDN outage — client/app origin pe fall back kar sake.
  • Invalidation — file jaldi hatani hai toh vendor ki invalidation API call karo, ya better, versioned URLs use karo (app.css?v=42 ya app.3f9a1c.css). Naya URL = naya object, toh invalidate karne ko kuch bacha hi nahi.

Stage 5 aur 6 ke baad web servers static files serve nahi karte, aur DB cache ke peeche protected hai.

docs.title: Stage 7 · Stateless web tier
docs.text:
Web servers ko freely add/remove karne ke liye (auto-scaling), koi bhi web server user ka state (jaise session) nahi rakh sakta.

Stateful — user A ka session server 1 ki memory mein hai. A ki har request server 1 pe hi jaani chahiye. LBs yeh sticky sessions se kar lete hain, par phir servers add/remove karna ya ek server khona sessions tod deta hai, aur load uneven bant-ta hai.

Stateless — session data ek shared store mein hai (Redis, NoSQL DB, ya RDBMS). Koi bhi server koi bhi request le sakta hai; servers interchangeable "cattle" hain, "pets" nahi.

flowchart LR
    U[Users] --> LB{{Load balancer}}
    LB --> W1[Web 1]
    LB --> W2[Web 2]
    LB --> W3[Web 3]
    W1 & W2 & W3 --> S[(Shared session store<br/>Redis / NoSQL)]

Ab auto-scaling bachchon ka khel hai: "agar average CPU 5 minute tak 70% se upar ho toh 2 servers add karo" jaisa rule seedha kaam karta hai, kyunki naye server ko purane servers se kuch nahi chahiye.

Thoda gehraai mein: sessions ki jagah tokens

Stateless hone ka ek aur tareeka hai state ko client mein rakhna: ek signed token (jaise JWT) jo har server shared key se verify kar sake, bina kisi lookup ke. Trade-off: token ko expiry se pehle revoke karna mushkil hai, isliye aksar short expiry + chhoti revocation list ke saath use hota hai.

docs.title: Stage 8 · Multiple data centers
docs.text:
Jab users duniya bhar mein phail jaate hain, ek data center ka matlab door ke users ke liye high latency, aur woh DC fail hua toh total outage. Toh hum do ya zyada chalate hain.

flowchart TB
    U[Users] --> G{{GeoDNS}}
    G -->|"x% (sabse paas)"| DC1
    G -->|"(100-x)%"| DC2
    subgraph DC1[Data center: US-East]
      LB1{{LB}} --> W1[Web tier] --> C1[(Cache)] & D1[(DB)]
    end
    subgraph DC2[Data center: US-West]
      LB2{{LB}} --> W2[Web tier] --> C2[(Cache)] & D2[(DB)]
    end
    D1 <-. async replication .-> D2
  • GeoDNS user ki location ke hisaab se domain ko alag IP mein resolve karta hai, aur usse sabse paas waale DC pe bhejta hai.
  • DC2 down hua toh DNS 100% traffic DC1 pe bhej deta hai.

Mushkil kya hai:

  1. Traffic redirection — users ko steer karne aur jaldi failover karne ke tools (GeoDNS, anycast, global LBs). DNS caching ki wajah se failover instant nahi hota; TTLs kam rakho.
  2. Data synchronisation — failover ke baad user jis DC mein pahunche, wahan uska data pehle se hona chahiye. Data DCs ke across replicate hota hai, usually asynchronously (toh disaster mein kuch seconds ke writes kho sakte hain). Netflix ka active-active multi-region setup famous example hai.
  3. Testing aur deployment — har DC mein same code aur config chalna chahiye. Automated deployment zaroori hai.

Active-passive vs active-active: active-passive mein doosra DC warm standby hai. Active-active mein dono live traffic serve karte hain — better utilisation aur tez failover, par same data pe do jagah concurrent writes handle karne padte hain.

docs.title: Stage 9 · Message queue
docs.text:
Kuch kaam slow hote hain (images resize karna, emails bhejna, video transcode karna) aur unhe user ki request block nahi karni chahiye. Message queue services ke beech ek durable buffer hai jo asynchronous communication enable karta hai.

  • Producers messages queue mein publish karte hain.
  • Consumers messages uthate hain aur kaam karte hain.
  • Dono ko ek hi time pe zinda hone ki zaroorat nahi → decoupling.
flowchart LR
    W[Web servers<br/>producers] -->|"job publish: photo 123 crop karo"| Q[[Message queue]]
    Q --> P1[Photo worker 1]
    Q --> P2[Photo worker 2]
    Q --> P3[Photo worker 3]
    P1 & P2 & P3 --> S[(Object storage)]

Example: ek photo app users ko crop, sharpen, blur karne deta hai. Web server bas queue mein job daal deta hai aur turant "processing…" reply kar deta hai. Workers apni speed se jobs uthate hain. Queue badhi toh workers add karo; mostly khaali rehti hai toh kuch hata do. Producers aur consumers alag-alag scale hote hain.

docs.title: Thoda gehraai mein
docs.text:
• Delivery guarantees. At-most-once (message kho sakta hai), at-least-once (duplicate ho sakta hai — common default), exactly-once (mehenga, limited). At-least-once ke saath consumers ko idempotent banao: same message do baar process ho toh bhi nuksaan na ho (message ID se dedupe).
  • Queue vs log. RabbitMQ/SQS-style queues consume hone ke baad message delete kar dete hain. Kafka ek log hai: messages retain hote hain, consumers apna offset track karte hain, kai consumer groups same stream replay kar sakte hain.
  • Backpressure. Queue depth key metric hai — depth badh rahi hai matlab consumers peeche reh gaye. Yeh auto-scaling ka natural signal bhi hai.
  • Dead-letter queue (DLQ). Jo messages baar-baar fail hote hain unhe side mein kar do, taaki baaki sab block na ho.

docs.title: Stage 10 · Logging, metrics, automation
docs.text:
Kuch servers pe yeh nice-to-have hain. Is scale pe zaroori.

  • Logging — har server ke error logs ek searchable jagah collect karo (ELK / OpenSearch, Loki, Cloud Logging).
  • Metrics teen levels pe:
    • Host: CPU, memory, disk I/O, network.
    • Aggregated/service: DB tier latency, cache hit ratio, queue depth, error rate.
    • Business: daily active users, retention, revenue, sign-ups.
  • Automation — CI (har commit automatically build aur test), CD (automated, repeatable deploys), infrastructure as code.

Four golden signals

Kisi bhi service ke liye dekho latency, traffic, errors aur saturation. Interview mein inka naam loge toh lagega tumne production systems chalaye hain.

docs.title: Stage 11 · Database scale karna: sharding
docs.text:
Data badhta ja raha hai, aur akela leader overloaded hai. Phir se do options.

Vertical: ek monster database server khareed lo. Cloud providers terabytes RAM waali machines dete hain, aur Stack Overflow saalon tak ~10M monthly visitors ke saath ek hi primary database pe chala. Par: hardware ki hard limit, phir bhi SPOF, aur bahut mehenga.

Horizontal = sharding: data ko kai databases (shards) mein tod do. Har shard ka schema same hai par har ek mein rows ka alag subset hai.

flowchart TB
    A[App] --> R{"shard = user_id % 4"}
    R -->|0| S0[(Shard 0<br/>users 0,4,8…)]
    R -->|1| S1[(Shard 1<br/>users 1,5,9…)]
    R -->|2| S2[(Shard 2<br/>users 2,6,10…)]
    R -->|3| S3[(Shard 3<br/>users 3,7,11…)]

docs.title: Shard key chunna (sabse important decision)
docs.text:
Shard key (partition key) decide karti hai row kis shard pe jaayegi. Achhi key:

  1. Data barabar baant-ti hai (high cardinality, koi skew nahi).
  2. Main query se match karti hai — common request ek shard pe jaaye, saare shards pe nahi.
  3. Kam badalti hai — row ko ek shard se doosre pe le jaana mehenga hai.

Common sharding strategies:

Strategy Kaise Fayda Nuksaan Hash-based hash(key) % N (ya consistent hashing) Barabar spread Range queries saare shards pe; N badla toh zyada data hilta hai Range-based A–F → shard 1, G–M → shard 2 … ya date se Range scans saste Hotspots (saara naya data latest shard pe) Directory / lookup Ek table key → shard map karti hai Flexible, rebalance easy Lookup service extra infra + SPOF ho sakti hai Geo-based India ke users → shard IN Data locality, data-residency laws Sizes uneven

docs.title: Sharding jo nayi problems laati hai
docs.text:
1. Resharding. Ek shard bhar gaya (growth) ya kuch shards jaldi bhar gaye (skew) → sharding function badalna padega aur data move karna padega. % N ke saath N badla toh lagbhag sab relocate hota hai. Consistent hashing (Chapter 5) sirf ~1/N keys move karke yeh fix karta hai.
  2. Celebrity / hotspot problem. Virat Kohli, Shah Rukh Khan aur Taylor Swift ek hi shard pe aa gaye toh reads se woh pighal jaayega. Fixes: hot keys ko dedicated shards do, hot key ko aur tod do (jaise celebrity_id#1..#10), aur aggressively cache karo.
  3. Shards ke across joins aur transactions. Shards ke across SQL join slow ya impossible hai, aur cross-shard transactions ko two-phase commit chahiye. Common workaround: denormalise — data aise store karo ki har query ek shard ki ek table se answer ho jaaye.

Aakhir mein, jo workloads ko relational features nahi chahiye (activity logs, session data, counters) unhe NoSQL stores mein le jao taaki relational database ka load kam ho.

docs.title: Final picture
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    U["Users (web + mobile)"] --> DNS{{GeoDNS}}
    U --> CDN[(CDN<br/>static assets)]
    DNS --> LB{{Load balancer}}
    subgraph DC["Data center (×2 ya zyada)"]
      LB --> W1[Web 1] & W2[Web 2] & W3[Web N]
      W1 & W2 & W3 --> CACHE[(Cache cluster)]
      W1 & W2 & W3 --> SESS[(Session store / NoSQL)]
      W1 & W2 & W3 --> SH0[(Shard 0<br/>leader + followers)] & SH1[(Shard 1<br/>leader + followers)]
      W1 & W2 & W3 --> MQ[[Message queue]] --> WK[Workers]
      MON[Logging · Metrics · Automation]
    end

Scaling checklist (yaad kar lo — aage ke har chapter ki vocabulary yahi hai):

  • Web tier stateless hai; state shared stores mein hai.
  • Har tier pe redundancy — koi important cheez sirf ek machine pe nahi chalti.
  • Reads aggressively cache karo; static assets CDN pe.
  • Databases replicate karo; ek leader kaafi na ho toh shard karo.
  • Geo-routing aur failover ke saath multiple data centers.
  • Queues se decouple karo; badi apps ko independent services mein todo.
  • Sab kuch monitor karo aur builds, tests, deploys automate karo.

docs.title: Trade-offs ek nazar mein
docs.text: Technique Kya milta hai Kya dena padta hai Load balancer Availability, horizontal scale Ek extra hop; LB khud redundant hona chahiye Replication Read scale, durability, failover Replication lag, failover complexity Cache Latency, DB ka load kam Staleness, invalidation bugs, stampedes CDN Global latency, origin ka load kam Per GB cost, invalidation Stateless tier Easy auto-scaling, resilience Ek shared state store chalana padta hai Multi-DC Disaster tolerance, kam global latency Cross-DC sync, failover pe data loss possible, ops cost Message queue Decoupling, spikes smooth Results baad mein, duplicates, ek aur system Sharding Write + storage scale Resharding, hotspots, cross-shard joins/transactions nahi

docs.title: Interviewer follow-ups
docs.text:
Tumhare read replicas 5 second peeche hain. User post edit karta hai aur turant purana version dekhta hai. Kya karoge?

Yeh async replication lag se hone waali read-your-own-writes problem hai. Options: (1) user ke write ke baad kuch seconds tak usi user ke reads leader pe bhejo; (2) write ke time leader ki log position note karo aur sirf un replicas se padho jo wahan tak pahunch gaye; (3) client-side state optimistically update kar do taaki UI naya version dikhaye. Batao ki replication ko synchronous karna bhi fix karega, par write latency aur availability kharab hogi.

Cache poora down ho gaya. Kya hoga aur database ko kaise bachaoge?

Har read DB read ban jaata hai — DB pe normal se 10–50× load aa sakta hai aur woh gir sakta hai (cascading failure). Bachav: cache ko zones ke across replicated cluster ki tarah chalao; DB ke raaste pe circuit breaker / rate limit lagao; full traffic bhejne se pehle naye cache ko warm karo; poora fail hone ki jagah degraded response do (jaise thoda stale feed).

Update pe cache key delete kyun karte ho, nayi value kyun nahi likhte?

Do concurrent writers interleave ho sakte hain: A ne DB=1 likha, B ne DB=2 likha, B ne cache=2 set kiya, A ne cache=1 set kiya → cache mein ab stale value hai aur expiry door tak nahi. Delete idempotent hai aur order se fark nahi padta: agla reader sahi value reload kar lega. (Concurrent reader ke saath chhota sa race ab bhi hai; TTL damage limit karta hai.)

E-commerce orders table ke liye shard key kaise chunoge?

Dominant queries dekho: "meri orders dikhao" (user_id se) aur "order X do" (order_id se). user_id se shard karne se user ki saari orders ek shard pe rehti hain (fast history page, scatter-gather nahi). Phir order ID mein shard embed kar do (ya chhota order_id → user_id lookup rakho) taaki direct lookup bhi ek shard pe jaaye. Bade B2B customers ka skew dhyaan rakho — unhe apna shard chahiye ho sakta hai.

Cache kab NAHI lagaoge?

Jab data write-heavy ho ya lagbhag har read pe badalta ho (hit ratio kam), jab strong consistency chahiye aur staleness chalegi hi nahi (transfer ke time account balance), ya jab DB already latency target meet kar raha ho — cache ek aur system aur bugs ki ek nayi category laata hai.

Sticky sessions vs shared session store — kaunsa aur kyun?

Shared store. Sticky sessions server fail hone pe toot jaate hain (users logout ho jaate hain), scale-in painful banate hain, aur load skew karte hain. Shared store (Redis cluster) har request pe ~1 ms add karta hai par servers interchangeable bana deta hai. Sticky sessions sirf short-lived, dobara banne waale state ke liye ya cache-locality optimisation ke liye theek hain.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
Inse bacho

  • 1,000 users waale system ke liye seedha "microservices + Kafka + Cassandra" pe kood jaana. Bataye gaye requirements tak scale karo.
  • Cache add karna bina bataye ki kya cache hoga, TTL kya hai, aur invalidate kaise hoga.
  • "Replicas add karo" bolna bina replication lag aur usse kya tootta hai bataye.
  • Shard key ka naam liye bina aur main query se justify kiye bina sharding karna.
  • Bhool jaana ki load balancer, cache aur queue ko bhi redundancy chahiye.
  • Cache ko database samajhna (data sirf memory mein).

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — Steps ka order

Ek startup ka single server 90% CPU pe hai. Database aur app same box pe hain, saari images app serve karta hai, aur sessions server memory mein hain. Pehle chaar changes kis order mein karoge, aur kyun?

Solution. 1. DB ko alag machine pe le jao — sabse bada turant relief; app aur DB ladna band. 2. Static images CDN / object storage pe daalo — app se bandwidth aur CPU ka bada hissa hat jaata hai. 3. Sessions Redis mein le jao — web tier stateless ho jaata hai, jo agle step ki shart hai… 4. Load balancer + doosra web server — horizontal scale aur web tier mein koi SPOF nahi. (Phir: DB ke aage cache, phir read replicas.)

Practice 2 — Cache sizing

Product catalog mein 50M products hain, average 2 KB each. 80% traffic top 10% products pe aata hai. Hot set cache karne ke liye kitni memory? 64 GB ke kitne cache nodes (30% headroom rakho)?

Solution. Hot set = 10% × 50M = 5M products × 2 KB = 10 GB. Overhead ke saath (keys, data-structure metadata, fragmentation ~1.5×) ≈ 15 GB. 30% headroom → ~21 GB. Ek 64 GB node mein fit, par kam se kam 2–3 nodes chalao (replicas / zones ke across) taaki ek node fail ho toh sab DB pe na gire.

Practice 3 — Hot shard

Tum tweets ko user_id se shard karte ho. 100M followers waala celebrity post karta hai aur uske shard ka CPU reads se 100% ho jaata hai. Teen mitigations batao.

Solution. (1) Celebrity ke recent tweets ko replicated cache tier mein cache karo taaki reads shard tak kam pahunchein. (2) Us hot shard ke liye specially read replicas badhao. (3) Hot key tod do — celebrity ko dedicated shard pe le jao, ya key ko salt karo (user_id#0..#9) taaki data kai shards mein phaile aur read pe fan-in karo. (Bonus: feeds ke liye celebrities ka fan-out-on-read path — Chapter 11 dekho.)

Practice 4 — Availability ka hisaab

Tumhari app ko LB, web tier aur DB teeno up chahiye. Har ek 99.9% available hai. Overall availability kya hai? Agar automatic failover ke saath do independent DB replicas chalao toh kya badlega?

Solution. Series mein: 0.999³ ≈ 99.7% (~26 ghante downtime/saal). Do DBs parallel mein: 1 − (0.001)² = 99.9999%, toh total ≈ 0.999 × 0.999 × 0.999999 ≈ 99.8%. Har tier pe redundancy hi number badhati hai — Chapter 2 ke widget mein try karo.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• DNS lookup se JSON response tak ek request trace kar sakta hoon.
  • SQL vs NoSQL ko buzzwords se nahi, access patterns se samjha sakta hoon, aur chaar NoSQL families bata sakta hoon.
  • Pata hai vertical scaling kyun deewar se takrata hai aur horizontal scaling ko kya chahiye.
  • 4 load-balancing algorithms aur L4 vs L7 samjha sakta hoon.
  • Leader–follower replication, failover, aur replication lag example ke saath samjha sakta hoon.
  • Cache-aside code likh sakta hoon aur 5 caching strategies compare kar sakta hoon; TTL, eviction, stampede fixes pata hain.
  • CDN content kaise serve karta hai, pull vs push, aur versioned URLs invalidation se better kyun hain — pata hai.
  • Web tier stateless kyun hona chahiye, samjha sakta hoon.
  • Multi-DC setup aur uski teen mushkil problems bata sakta hoon.
  • Message queue kya deta hai, delivery guarantees, aur consumers idempotent kyun hone chahiye — pata hai.
  • Sharding strategies compare kar sakta hoon, shard key chun sakta hoon, aur resharding, hotspots, joins samjha sakta hoon.

Aage: 02 · Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation

docs.title: 02 · Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
docs.text:
⏱ 35 min read 🔥 Lagbhag har design round mein poocha jaata hai Book: Chapter 2

TL;DR

  • Estimation ka matlab exact answer nahi — matlab hai saaf process dikhana aur sahi order of magnitude pe pahunchna (10× ka fark matter karta hai, 20% ka nahi).
  • Teen tables zubaani yaad rakho: powers of two (KB→PB), latency numbers (memory ≈ 100 ns, SSD ≈ 100 µs, cross-continent ≈ 150 ms), aur availability nines (99.9% ≈ saal mein 8.8 ghante down).
  • Core recipe: DAU × actions per user ÷ 86,400 = average QPS, peak ke liye × 2–3. Storage = writes/day × size × retention × replicas.
  • Bindaas round karo (86,400 ≈ 10⁵), assumptions likh lo, aur har jagah units likho.
  • Numbers se decisions lo: "40K QPS reads → cache chahiye", "55 PB → object storage chahiye, DB nahi".

docs.title: Intuition: estimate karte hi kyun hain?
docs.text:
Civil engineer jab pul (bridge) plan karta hai, toh paint ka colour pehle nahi chunta. Pehle poochta hai: kitne trucks, kitne bhaari, kitni baar? Jawab decide karta hai ki footbridge chahiye ya steel ka suspension bridge.

Software mein estimation yahi kaam karta hai. "Twitter design karo" ka matlab 3 servers bhi ho sakta hai aur 3,000 bhi — aur dono bilkul alag designs hain. Paanch minute ka hisaab batata hai ki tum kaunsa bana rahe ho, aur interviewer ko dikhata hai ki tum requirements se design karte ho, buzzwords se nahi.

docs.title: Table 1 · Powers of two
docs.text:
Data sizes powers of 2 hote hain, par estimation ke liye inhe powers of 10 maan lo — error 10% se kam hai.

Power Exact value ≈ Naam Short 2¹⁰ 1,024 1 hazaar Kilobyte KB 2²⁰ 1,048,576 10 lakh (1 million) Megabyte MB 2³⁰ 1,073,741,824 100 crore (1 billion) Gigabyte GB 2⁴⁰ ≈ 1.1 × 10¹² 1 trillion Terabyte TB 2⁵⁰ ≈ 1.1 × 10¹⁵ 1 quadrillion Petabyte PB

Roz ki cheezon ka size (roughly yaad rakho):

Cheez Size 1 ASCII character 1 byte Ek long / Snowflake ID / timestamp 8 bytes Ek UUID 16 bytes (string mein 36) Tweet jitna text (280 chars) ~300 bytes Metadata ki typical DB row 100 B – 1 KB Compressed photo 200 KB – 2 MB 1080p video ka 1 minute ~50–100 MB raw upload, har streamed rendition ~10–20 MB

docs.title: Table 2 · Latency numbers jo har programmer ko pata hone chahiye
docs.text:
Yeh Jeff Dean ki famous list se hain (lagbhag 2010, aaj ke approximations ke saath). Hardware improve hone se exact values badalti rehti hain; ratios matter karte hain.

Operation Approx. time Aise socho… L1 cache reference 0.5–1 ns — Branch mispredict 3–5 ns — L2 cache reference 4–7 ns — Mutex lock/unlock ~25 ns — Main memory reference ~100 ns "fast" ka baseline 1 KB compress (Snappy/zstd) ~2–3 µs sasta — bhejne se pehle compress karo! 1 Gbps network pe 1 KB bhejna ~10 µs — SSD se random read ~16–100 µs memory se ~1,000× slow Memory se 1 MB sequential read ~5–10 µs — Same data center ke andar round trip ~0.5 ms — SSD se 1 MB sequential read ~50 µs – 1 ms — Disk (HDD) seek ~2–10 ms random seeks se bacho! HDD se 1 MB sequential read ~1–5 ms — Packet round trip CA → Netherlands → CA ~150 ms speed of light hi limit hai

Units: 1 ns = 10⁻⁹ s · 1 µs = 1,000 ns · 1 ms = 1,000 µs = 10⁶ ns.

Insaani time mein socho — agar ek memory reference 1 second leta: toh SSD read lagbhag 1–2 din, disk seek lagbhag 3 mahine, aur cross-continent round trip lagbhag 5 saal leta. Isliye caches aur data locality itne important hain.

Interview mein yeh takeaways zor se bolo:

  1. Memory tez, disk slow → hot data RAM mein cache karo.
  2. Disk seeks se bacho → sequential I/O prefer karo (isi liye LSM-trees aur append-only logs bane — Chapter 6).
  3. Compression sasta hai → network pe bhejne se pehle compress karo.
  4. Cross-region calls mehenge hain (~100+ ms) → baatooni calls ek data center ke andar rakho; data users ke paas replicate karo.

docs.title: Table 3 · Availability numbers ("nines")
docs.text:
Availability = kitne fraction time system chal raha hai. Service Level Agreement (SLA) woh promise hai jo provider customers se karta hai (AWS, GCP aur Azure zyada tar compute SLAs 99.9% ya upar rakhte hain). Related terms: SLO tumhara internal target hai, SLI actual measured value.

Availability Downtime / din Downtime / hafta Downtime / mahina Downtime / saal 99% ("two nines") 14.4 min 1.68 h 7.31 h 3.65 din 99.9% ("three nines") 1.44 min 10.1 min 43.8 min 8.77 h 99.99% ("four nines") 8.64 s 1.01 min 4.38 min 52.6 min 99.999% ("five nines") 864 ms 6.05 s 26.3 s 5.26 min 99.9999% ("six nines") 86.4 ms 605 ms 2.63 s 31.6 s

Availability jodna:

  • Series mein (saare parts chahiye): multiply karo. Teen 99.9% parts → 0.999³ ≈ 99.7%. Har dependency availability ghatati hai.
  • Parallel mein (koi ek kaafi hai): 1 − (1 − a)ⁿ. Do 99% replicas → 1 − 0.01² = 99.99%. Redundancy availability badhati hai.

Khud try karo:

docs.title: Kaam ke conversions
docs.text: Fact Yeh use karo Ek din mein seconds = 86,400 ≈ 10⁵ (division aasaan) Ek mahine mein seconds ≈ 2.5 × 10⁶ Ek saal mein seconds ≈ 3 × 10⁷ 10 lakh (1 million) requests/din ≈ 12 QPS 100 crore (1 billion) requests/din ≈ 12,000 QPS 1 request/sec lagatar ≈ 86K/din ≈ 2.6M/mahina

docs.title: Core recipes
docs.text:
DAU                = MAU × (roz active hone ka fraction)
Average QPS        = DAU × (per user per day requests) / 86,400
Peak QPS           = Average QPS × (2 … 5)          ← traffic flat nahi hota
Read vs write QPS  = read:write ratio se split karo
Storage per day    = (writes per day) × (bytes per write)
Total storage      = storage per day × 365 × years × replication factor
Bandwidth          = QPS × bytes per request          (writes ke liye ingress, reads ke liye egress)
Cache memory       = daily read data ka ~20%          (80/20 rule: 20% items ko 80% reads milte hain)
Servers            = Peak QPS / (ek server kitna QPS sambhale)  + headroom

Rule-of-thumb capacities (bahut rough, ek commodity server ke liye):

Component Ballpark Stateless web/app server 1K – 10K simple requests/sec Relational DB (single primary) ~1K – 10K writes/sec, achhe indexes ke saath reads zyada Redis / Memcached node ~100K+ ops/sec Kafka broker ~100K+ messages/sec Commodity server RAM 64 – 512 GB

docs.title: Interactive calculator
docs.text: Koi bhi input badlo, poori chain dobara calculate hoti hai. Defaults neeche Worked Example 1 se match karte hain (100 KB average write hai: 20% posts × 500 KB image).

docs.title: Worked example 1 · Ek microblogging service
docs.text:
(Numbers practice ke liye banaye hue hain.)

Assumptions — pehle board pe likho:

  • 400 M monthly active users, 40% roz use karte hain.
  • Har daily user 3 posts publish karta hai aur ~80 posts padhta hai (timeline loads).
  • 20% posts mein ~500 KB ki image hai (video abhi ignore).
  • Sab kuch 7 saal rakhna hai.

QPS

  • DAU = 400 M × 40% = 160 M
  • Write QPS = 160 M × 3 / 86,400 ≈ 480 M / 10⁵ ≈ 4,800 posts/sec; peak (×2) ≈ ~10,000
  • Read QPS = 160 M × 80 / 10⁵ ≈ 128,000 post reads/sec → read-heavy (~27:1) → caching aur precomputed timelines zaroori (Chapter 11).

Storage

  • Har post ka text + metadata: id 8 B + author id 8 B + text ~300 B + timestamps/counters ~100 B ≈ ~0.5 KB
  • Text/din = 480 M posts × 0.5 KB = 240 GB/din → ×365×7 ≈ ~0.6 PB (replication se pehle)
  • Media/din = 480 M × 20% × 500 KB = 48 TB/din → ×365×7 ≈ ~123 PB

Numbers kya bata rahe hain: media text se ~200× bhaari hai. Text sharded database mein jaayega; media object storage (S3) + CDN mein. Yeh ek observation poore architecture ko shape karta hai.

docs.title: Worked example 2 · WhatsApp jaisa chat
docs.text:
Assumptions: 2 B MAU, 50% daily → 1 B DAU; har user 40 messages/din bhejta hai; average message ~100 bytes; messages server pe 30 din store (deliver/backup hone tak).

  • Messages/din = 1 B × 40 = 40 B/din
  • Average write QPS = 40 B / 10⁵ = 400,000 msgs/sec; peak ×3 ≈ 1.2 M/sec
  • Storage/din = 40 B × 100 B = 4 TB/din → 30 din ≈ 120 TB, ×3 replicas ≈ 360 TB
  • Connections: peak pe 30% DAU online → 300 M concurrent WebSocket connections. Ek achhe se tuned server pe ~1 M connections → sirf connections sambhalne ke liye ~300+ chat servers (plus headroom).
