Decision: bottleneck storage nahi, concurrent connections aur message fan-out hai → stateful chat servers + writes ke liye optimised key-value store (Chapter 12).

docs.title: Worked example 3 · YouTube jaisa video
docs.text:
Assumptions: 2 B MAU, 50% daily → 1 B DAU; har user 5 videos/din dekhta hai; 1% users 1 video/din upload karte hain; average upload 300 MB (raw); hum ~4 renditions store karte hain jo milke raw ka ~1.5× hain.

  • View QPS = 1 B × 5 / 10⁵ = 50,000 views/sec
  • Uploads/din = 1 B × 1% = 10 M videos/din → ~115 uploads/sec
  • Storage/din = 10 M × 300 MB × 1.5 ≈ 4.5 PB/din (!)
  • Egress: agar average view 100 MB stream karta hai → 5 B views × 100 MB = 500 PB/din serve — yeh sirf CDN kar sakta hai.

Decision: cost pe CDN egress aur storage haavi hain. Optimisations — sirf popular videos CDN se, better compression, unpopular videos ke kam renditions — first-class design topics ban jaate hain (Chapter 14).

docs.title: Worked example 4 · URL shortener
docs.text:
Assumptions: roz 40 M naye short links; har link apni zindagi mein ~50 baar khulta hai (read:write = 50:1); links 15 saal rakhne hain; har record ~250 bytes (long URL + code + owner + timestamps).

  • Write QPS = 40 M / 10⁵ ≈ 400/sec (exactly ~460)
  • Read QPS = ×50 ≈ 20,000–23,000/sec; peak ×2 ≈ ~45K/sec
  • 15 saal mein records = 40 M × 365 × 15 ≈ 219 B records
  • Storage = 219 B × 250 B ≈ 55 TB (replication se pehle)
  • Short-code length: kam se kam 219 B unique codes chahiye. Base-62: 62⁶ ≈ 57 B (kam), 62⁷ ≈ 3.5 T ✓ → 7 characters.

Decision: chhote records, bahut zyada count, reads ≫ writes → sharded key-value store plus hot links ke liye aggressive cache. (Poora design Chapter 8 mein.)

docs.title: Worked example 5 · Instagram jaisi photos — cache & servers
docs.text:
Assumptions: 500 M DAU; har user 50 photos/din dekhta hai; 0.2 photos/din upload karta hai, 2 MB ki; har photo ka metadata 1 KB; ek server 2,000 QPS handle karta hai.

  • Read QPS = 500 M × 50 / 10⁵ = 250,000/sec; peak ×2 = 500K/sec
  • Write QPS = 500 M × 0.2 / 10⁵ = 1,000 uploads/sec
  • Photo storage/din = 100 M × 2 MB = 200 TB/din
  • Metadata cache: roz 25 B photo views; par unique photos jo dekhi gayi woh kahin kam. Agar hot set pichle 30 din ki photos ka ~20% hai: 100 M × 30 × 20% × 1 KB ≈ 600 GB → 64 GB ke ~10 cache nodes (headroom/replicas ke saath).
  • API servers: 500K / 2,000 = peak pe 250 servers, + ~30% headroom ≈ 325.

docs.title: Tips jo interviewer ko impress karte hain
docs.text:
Interview mein estimate kaise karein

  1. Pehle assumptions bolo, aur confirm karo: "Main 100 M DAU maan raha hoon — theek lag raha hai?"
  2. Bindaas round karo. 48,213 × 6.8 → 50,000 × 7 = 350,000. Koi decimal precision expect nahi karta.
  3. Har unit likho. "5" ka koi matlab nahi; "5 MB/s" ka hai.
  4. Reads aur writes alag karo — dono alag components ki taraf le jaate hain (cache vs write-optimised storage).
  5. Numbers ko decisions mein badlo — "toh writes ek DB sambhal lega, par reads ko cache chahiye".
  6. Sanity-check karo kisi jaani-pehchaani cheez se: "global chat app ke liye 1.2 M msgs/sec plausible hai."
  7. Zyada time mat lagao. 3–5 minute, phir design pe chalo.

Aksar poochhe jaane waale estimates

QPS aur peak QPS · N saal mein storage · bandwidth (ingress/egress) · cache memory · servers / connections ki ginti · ID space (kitne bits / characters).

docs.title: Interviewer follow-ups
docs.text:
Peak ke liye 2–5 se multiply kyun? Yeh arbitrary nahi hai?

Traffic daily cycles (shaam ka peak), weekly cycles aur events (cricket final, New Year, sale) follow karta hai. Consumer apps ke liye 2–3× peak-to-average common hai; event-driven spikes 10×+ ho sakte hain. Point yeh hai ki average nahi, peak ke liye design karo — aur batao multiplier kyun chuna ("user base India-heavy hai, toh shaam ka peak").

Tumhara storage estimate 55 PB hai. Design mein kya badlega?

Koi database itna economically nahi rakhega. Blobs ke liye object storage (S3/GCS/HDFS), database mein sirf metadata (URLs, owners, sizes), purana data cold storage pe (sasta, slow), identical uploads deduplicate karo, aur reads CDN se bhejo.

Kitna cache chahiye, yeh kaise estimate karoge?

80/20 rule: ~20% objects ko ~80% reads milte hain. Cache memory ≈ 20% × (roz padhe gaye unique objects) × object size. Phir overhead (~1.3–1.5× keys aur metadata ke liye) aur replicas jodo. Baad mein real hit-ratio metrics se validate karo.

1 B requests/din — kya yeh bahut hai?

Average ~12K QPS, peak pe shayad 30K — bada hai, par bilkul manageable: kuch dozen stateless servers, ek cache cluster, aur ek sharded/replicated DB. "Per day" ko "per second" mein badalna sabse tez tareeka hai yeh samajhne ka ki number kitna darawna hai.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — Food delivery

India mein ek food-delivery app: 20 M DAU, har user din mein 4 baar app kholta hai aur har baar 10 API calls hoti hain. Orders: 3 M/din. Har order 5 KB likhta hai. 3 saal rakhna hai. Dinner pe peak average ka 4× hai. API peak QPS, order write QPS, aur 3× replication ke saath order storage nikalo.

Solution. API: 20 M × 4 × 10 = 800 M/din → 800 M / 10⁵ = 8K QPS avg, ×4 = 32K peak. Orders: 3 M / 10⁵ ≈ 35/sec avg (~140 peak) — DB ke liye kuch bhi nahi. Storage: 3 M × 5 KB = 15 GB/din × 365 × 3 ≈ 16.4 TB × 3 replicas ≈ ~50 TB. Takeaway: API read path (menus, restaurant lists) ko caching chahiye; order writes aasaan hain.

Practice 2 — Snowflake bits

41-bit millisecond timestamp kitne saal ke IDs deta hai?

Solution. 2⁴¹ ms ≈ 2.2 × 10¹² ms ≈ 2.2 × 10⁹ s ≈ 2.2 × 10⁹ / 3.15 × 10⁷ ≈ ~69.7 saal (Chapter 7).

Practice 3 — Bandwidth

Ek video platform 50K concurrent streams 5 Mbps each pe serve karta hai. Egress kitna?

Solution. 50,000 × 5 Mbps = 250,000 Mbps = 250 Gbps ≈ 31 GB/s. Ek din mein ≈ 2.7 PB. CDN chahiye.

Practice 4 — Connections

Ek multiplayer game ke 10 M DAU hain; peak pe 10% online, har ek ek WebSocket rakhta hai. Ek gateway server 200K connections rakhta hai. Kitne gateway servers?

Solution. 10 M × 10% = 1 M connections / 200K = 5 servers; N+2 redundancy aur headroom ke saath → 7–8.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• KB se PB tak powers-of-two table likh sakta hoon.
  • Memory ≈ 100 ns, SSD ≈ 100 µs, HDD seek ≈ 10 ms, cross-continent ≈ 150 ms yaad hai — aur 4 takeaways bhi.
  • 99%, 99.9%, 99.99%, 99.999% ka downtime/saal pata hai, aur series vs parallel kaise jodte hain.
  • Per-day ko per-second turant badal sakta hoon (÷ 10⁵) aur pata hai 1 M/din ≈ 12 QPS.
  • QPS, peak, storage, bandwidth, cache size aur server count units ke saath estimate kar sakta hoon.
  • Har number ko design decision mein badal sakta hoon.

Aage: 03 · Interview ka Framework

docs.title: 03 · System Design Interview ka Framework
docs.text:
⏱ 35 min read 🔥 Har case study mein yahi method use hoga Book: Chapter 3

TL;DR

  • Interview do colleagues ka milke ek vague problem solve karna simulate karta hai. Final diagram se zyada process matter karta hai.
  • 4 steps: (1) samjho & scope karo (~5–8 min) → (2) high-level design + buy-in (~10–15 min) → (3) deep dive (~15–20 min) → (4) wrap up (~3–5 min).
  • Kabhi seedha solution pe mat koodo. Features, users, scale, growth, constraints poochho. Jawab likh lo.
  • Deep dive interviewer ko steer karne do, par problem ke 2–3 sabse mushkil hisse pehle se tayyar rakho.
  • Red flags: over-engineering, chup rehna, ziddi hona, trade-offs ignore karna, chhoti baaton mein kho jaana.

docs.title: Interviewer asal mein kya judge kar raha hai
docs.text:
Koi expect nahi karta ki tum 45 minute mein YouTube design kar do — hazaaron engineers ko saal lage. Toh test kya ho raha hai?

Signal Strong ho toh kaisa dikhta hai Ambiguity handle karna "Chat app design karo" ko numbers ke saath ek saaf, agreed scope mein badal dete ho. Achhe sawaal Tumhare sawaal design badal dete hain ("sirf 1:1, ya 500 logon ke groups?"). Technical design Sensible components, saaf data flow, caches/queues/DBs ka sahi use. Trade-off thinking Alternatives batate ho aur kyun ek chuna — aur uski keemat kya hai. Depth Ek component pe dabaav pade toh 2–3 level aur andar ja sakte ho. Communication & collaboration Zor se sochte ho, check-in karte ho, hints achhe se lete ho. Pragmatism Bataye gaye scale ke liye design karte ho, by default Google-scale ke liye nahi.

Red flags jo interviewer note karta hai

  • Over-engineering — 10K users ke liye 12 microservices aur Kafka. Complexity ki asli, badhti hui keemat hoti hai.
  • Problem samajhne se pehle solution pe koodna.
  • Tang nazariya / zid — saaf counter-argument ke baad bhi apni choice defend karte rehna.
  • Lambi khamoshi — jo interviewer sun nahi sakta, use score nahi kar sakta.
  • Buzzword soup — "scalability ke liye microservices aur NoSQL use karenge", bina kisi reason ke.

docs.title: 4-step framework
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S1["① Samjho<br/>& scope<br/>5–8 min"] --> S2["② High-level<br/>design + buy-in<br/>10–15 min"]
    S2 --> S3["③ Deep dive<br/>15–20 min"]
    S3 --> S4["④ Wrap up<br/>3–5 min"]
    S2 -. feedback .-> S1
    S3 -. feedback .-> S2

Times 45-minute session ke hisaab se hain. Peeche jaate arrows important hain: zyada seekhte hue tum aksar scope ya high-level design revise karoge — yeh normal aur achha hai.

docs.title: Step 1 · Problem samjho aur scope tay karo
docs.text:
Woh student mat bano jo sabse pehle jawab chilla deta hai. Design interview mein bina samjhe speed negative signal hai. Dheere chalo, poochho, aur jawab board pe likho.

Jab tum poochte ho, interviewer ya toh jawab deta hai ya bolta hai "tum decide karo". Doosre case mein assumption bolo aur likh lo — baad mein refer karoge.

docs.title: Question bank
docs.text:
Relevant waale chuno — saare ek saath machine-gun mat karo.

Features (functional)ScaleQuality (non-functional)Constraints
  • Core features kaunse banane hain? Kya explicitly scope se bahar hai?
  • Users kaun hain — consumers, businesses, internal teams? Web, mobile, ya dono?
  • Sabse important user journey kya hai? (jaise "photo post karna" aur "apna feed dekhna")
  • Koi special requirement: search? notifications? analytics? edit/delete?
  • Kitne users (MAU/DAU)? Kitne concurrent?
  • Read:write ratio? Typical object ka size?
  • Kitni tezi se badh rahe hain? 3 / 6 / 12 mahine mein expected scale?
  • Traffic spiky hai (sales, live events) ya smooth? Global ya ek region?
  • Latency target? (jaise reads ke liye p99 < 200 ms)
  • Availability target? Thodi der down rehna chalega, ya thoda stale rehna?
  • Consistency — kya har read ko latest write dikhna zaroori hai? (bank balance vs like count)
  • Durability — kya kabhi data kho sakte hain? Kitne time tak rakhna hai?
  • Existing tech stack ya services jo reuse kar sakein (auth, payments, blob store)?
  • Budget / cost sensitivity? On-prem ya cloud?
  • Legal: data residency, privacy (GDPR / DPDP), content moderation?

docs.title: Jawabon ko requirements sheet mein badlo
docs.text:
"Photo-sharing app design karo" ke liye ek chhoti scoping baatcheet kuch aisi ho sakti hai — dhyaan do, har jawab design ki ek branch kaat deta hai:

Ek achhi scoping baatcheet (photo sharing)

Tum: Post kaun karta hai — koi bhi, ya sirf verified creators? — Interviewer: Koi bhi. Tum: Core actions? — I: Caption ke saath photo upload, logon ko follow karna, home feed scroll karna. Tum: Home feed ranked hai ya chronological? — I: Abhi ke liye chronological. Tum: Kitna bada? — I: 50M DAU; typical user kuch dino mein ek baar upload karta hai par feed din mein ~8 baar kholta hai. Tum: Max photo size, aur originals rakhne hain? — I: 10 MB tak; originals aur resized versions dono. Tum: Koi users jinke bahut zyada followers hain? — I: Haan, kuch accounts ke crore se zyada followers hain.

"Chronological" ranking service hata deta hai. "Crore se zyada followers" warning hai ki pure fan-out-on-write dard dega. "Originals + resized" matlab async image-processing pipeline, object storage aur CDN.

Result board pe likho — yeh interviewer ke saath tumhara contract hai:

FUNCTIONAL
  1. Photo upload (≤10 MB) + caption
  2. Follow / unfollow
  3. Followed accounts ka home feed, naya pehle
NON-FUNCTIONAL
  - 50M DAU; feed p99 < 300 ms; upload dikhne mein kuch second lag sakte hain
  - Feed ke liye consistency se zyada availability; uploaded photo kabhi na khoye
OUT OF SCOPE
  - Ranking, stories, DMs, ads
ESTIMATES (Ch. 2)
  - Feed loads ≈ 50M × 8 / 10^5 = 4K QPS avg, ~10K peak
  - Uploads ≈ 50M × 0.3 / 10^5 = 150/s; 15M/din × ~3 MB stored (orig + sizes) ≈ 45 TB/din

docs.title: Step 2 · High-level design propose karo aur buy-in lo
docs.text:
Goal: deep jaane se pehle ek blueprint jis pe dono agree karo.

  1. Boxes sketch karo: clients → (DNS/CDN) → load balancer → services → cache → databases → queues/workers → object storage.
  2. Ek request ko usme se chalao — "user upload karta hai: app pre-signed URL leta hai, seedha blob storage pe upload karta hai, phir POST /photos call karta hai…" Concrete use cases missing hisse dikha dete hain.
  3. Estimates se sanity-check — "peak pe 10K QPS feed reads — cache-backed feed service ke liye theek hai."
  4. Feedback maango — "Aage gehraai mein jaane se pehle kya yeh direction sahi lag rahi hai?" Interviewer ko teammate samjho.

docs.title: APIs aur data model — daalein ya nahi?
docs.text:
Problem pe depend karta hai. "Web search design karo" ke liye yeh bahut low-level hai. "URL shortener" ya "multiplayer game backend" ke liye API aur schema hi design hain. Doubt ho toh 2–4 core APIs sketch kar do:

POST /v1/photos/upload-url  → 200 { upload_url, photo_id }     # object storage ka pre-signed URL
POST /v1/photos             { photo_id, caption }  → 201
GET  /v1/feed?cursor=...    → 200 { items[], next_cursor }

aur 2–3 core tables:

users(user_id PK, handle, ...)
photos(photo_id PK, owner_id, caption, storage_key, created_at)
follows(follower_id, followee_id, created_at)   PK(follower_id, followee_id)

docs.title: Example: photo-sharing ka high-level design
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|1. upload URL lo| API[API servers]
    C -->|2. bytes PUT karo| OBJ[(Object storage)]
    C -->|3. POST /photos| API
    API --> META[(Photo + follow DB)]
    API -->|new photo event| Q[[Queue]]
    Q --> IMG[Resize workers] --> OBJ
    Q --> FAN[Feed builder] --> FC[(Feed cache)]
    C -->|feed padho| API --> FC
    OBJ --> CDN[(CDN)] --> C

Upload path aur feed path alag hain, aur bhaari kaam (resizing, feed building) queue ke peeche asynchronously hota hai. Agreement ke liye itni detail kaafi hai — feeds ka gehraai waala kaam Chapter 11 mein.

docs.title: Step 3 · Design deep dive
docs.text:
Ab tak scope agree ho chuka, blueprint ban chuka, feedback mil chuka. Ab jahan zaroori ho wahan gehraai mein jao.

Deep dive ke liye kya chunein:

  1. Interviewer ke peeche chalo. Agar woh pooche "celebrity ke liye fan-out kaise chalega?", wahi tumhara deep dive hai.
  2. Warna woh chuno jo is problem mein unique hai — jo isse yeh system banata hai, koi generic CRUD app nahi:
Problem Typical deep dives URL shortener Hash/encode function, collisions, 301 vs 302, cache Rate limiter Algorithm choice, distributed counters, race conditions Chat WebSockets, message ordering/IDs, online presence, multi-device sync News feed Fan-out on write vs read, celebrity problem, feed cache Web crawler URL frontier (politeness + priority), dedup, traps YouTube Upload + transcoding pipeline, CDN cost, streaming protocols Google Drive Block-level sync, conflict resolution, consistency, notifications
  1. Seniority se focus badalta hai. Junior: sahi components aur data flow. Senior: bottlenecks, capacity numbers, failure modes, operational concerns, cost.

Time management: kisi aisi cheez pe 10 minute jalana aasaan hai jo kuch dikhaati nahi (jaise ranking algorithm ka maths detail mein samjhana). Khud se poochte raho: kya isse dikh raha hai ki main scalable system design kar sakta hoon?

docs.title: Step 4 · Wrap up
docs.text:
Interviewer open-ended follow-ups pooch sakta hai ya tumhe chunne de sakta hai. Inse breadth dikhao:

  • Bottlenecks & improvements — "Single fan-out queue bottleneck hai; main ise user_id se partition karunga." Kabhi mat bolo ki design perfect hai.
  • Recap — 30 second mein design aur key trade-offs summarise karo. Khaaskar tab kaam ka jab tum kai raaston pe gaye ho.
  • Failure cases — server crash, network partition, cache loss, DC outage. Kya degrade hoga, kya khoyega?
  • Operations — metrics, logging, alerting, deployment/rollback.
  • Agla 10× scale — "100M DAU pe main post DB ko post_id se shard karunga aur doosra region add karunga."
  • Aur refinements — security, abuse/rate limiting, cost.

docs.title: Aadatein jo score karti hain — aur jo nuksaan karti hain
docs.text:
Score karne waali aadatein

  • Har assumption ko tab tak sawaal samjho jab tak interviewer confirm na kare.
  • Kuch bhi draw karne se pehle requirements dohra ke bolo.
  • Yaad rakho "sahi" design context pe depend karta hai — 5 logon ka startup aur hyperscaler alag decisions lete hain.
  • Apni reasoning bolte jao; interviewer wahi grade karta hai jo sunta hai.
  • Jab asli fork ho, dono raaste batao, ek chuno, aur uski keemat bolo.
  • Blueprint agree hone ke baad sabse risky component pe pehle time do.
  • Interviewer ko collaborator ki tarah use karo — unke hints free signal hain.
  • Atak jao toh bhi chalte raho; zor se reasoning karne pe bhi credit milta hai.

Nuksaan karne waali aadatein

  • Common problems practice kiye bina pahunch jaana.
  • Poochne se pehle draw karna.
  • Ek box ko detail mein chamakana jab baaki system abhi khaali hai.
  • Hint maangne ki jagah chup-chaap atke rehna.
  • Pehle diagram ko "done" samajhna — jab tak interviewer session band na kare, check-in karte raho.

docs.title: Poora mock walkthrough: "Pastebin design karo"
docs.text:
Chaaro steps ka ek compressed example, taaki rhythm samajh aaye.

Step 1 — Scope (6 min)

Tum: Users text paste karte hain aur shareable link milta hai — core yahi hai? Accounts, editing, syntax highlighting chahiye? I: Core hai paste + share link. Optional expiry. Editing nahi. Accounts optional. Tum: Per paste size limit? — I: Max 1 MB, zyada tar kuch KB. Tum: Scale? — I: 5M naye pastes/din, reads writes ke 10×. Tum: Kya links hamesha chalne chahiye? — I: Default expiry 1 saal, user chhoti chun sakta hai.

Board: FR: paste banao (≤1 MB, optional expiry), link se padho. NFR: high read availability, low read latency, pastes immutable. Estimates: writes 5M/10⁵ ≈ 60 QPS; reads ≈ 600 QPS (peak ~1.5K). Storage: 5M × 10 KB avg = 50 GB/din → 18 TB/saal.

Step 2 — High-level design (12 min) 

flowchart LR
    C[Client] --> LB{{LB}} --> API[Paste service]
    API -->|metadata| DB[(Metadata DB<br/>id, s3_key, expiry, owner)]
    API -->|content| S3[(Object storage)]
    API --> R[(Cache: hot pastes)]
    CL[Cleanup job] --> DB & S3
POST /pastes {content, expiry} → 7-char ID banao (unique ID ka base-62 — Ch. ⅞ dekho), content object storage mein, metadata DB mein, link return. GET /{id} → cache → DB → object storage. Immutable data = cache karna bahut aasaan; popular pastes CDN ke peeche. Tum: "Kya yeh sahi lag raha hai? Aage main ID generation aur expiry mein jaana chahunga."

Step 3 — Deep dive (18 min)
  • ID generation: random 7-char base-62 ka space 3.5 T hai; 1.8 B IDs/saal ke saath har insert pe collision ka chance bahut kam par zero nahi → unique numeric ID (Snowflake/ticket range) lo phir base-62 encode karo → na collision, na DB check.
  • Expiry: expires_at store karo; reads isse check karein (lazy delete); daily batch job expired rows aur S3 objects delete kare. Bulk cleanup ke liye S3 lifecycle rules.
  • Hot pastes: social media pe share hua paste minutes mein 100K hits laata hai → CDN, Cache-Control: max-age = min(bachi hui expiry, 1 din).
  • Abuse: per IP creates pe rate limit (Ch. 4); size limit LB pe.
Step 4 — Wrap up (4 min)

"Recap: stateless paste service, metadata paste_id se keyed sharded KV/SQL store mein, content object storage mein, reads ke liye cache + CDN. 10× pe bottleneck metadata writes honge → paste_id se shard. Failure: object storage slow ho toh cache/CDN se serve karenge; p99 read latency, 4xx/5xx, cache hit ratio monitor karenge. Aage async event stream se analytics add karunga."

docs.title: Kaam ke phrases
docs.text: Situation Kuch aisa bolo Shuruaat "Design karne se pehle main kuch requirements clarify karna chahunga." Assume karna "Main X maan raha hoon — likh leta hoon; galat ho toh batana." Chunna "Yahan do options hain: A aur B. A se milta hai…, keemat hai…; hamara load read-heavy hai toh main A lunga." Check-in "Itni detail theek hai, ya kahin aur gehraai mein jaun?" Atak gaye "Yahan best approach ke baare mein sure nahi hoon — zor se reason karke dekhta hoon." Hint lena "Achha point hai — isse cheezein badalti hain. Yeh hissa revise karta hoon." Wrap up "Main design aur main trade-offs recap karta hoon, phir bottlenecks pe baat karte hain."

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice 1 — Scope likho

Prompt: "Ek shehar ke liye parking-lot reservation system design karo." 6 clarifying questions aur ek requirements sheet likho (FR, NFR, out of scope) assumed numbers ke saath.

Sample answer. Sawaal: Users kaun — drivers, lot operators, dono? Pehle se reserve ya sirf real-time? Kitne lots/spots? Peak times? Payments scope mein? Kya reserved spot guaranteed hona chahiye (double booking nahi)? FR: location/time se spots search, reserve, cancel, pay; operators inventory manage karein. NFR: booking pe strong consistency (double-booking nahi), search thoda stale chalega, p99 search < 300 ms. Out: dynamic pricing, navigation. Numbers: 2,000 lots × 200 spots = 400K spots; 1M reservations/din → ~12 writes/sec avg, office hours mein 10× peaks.

Practice 2 — Red flags pakdo

Ek candidate ko "internal company tool ke liye URL shortener (5K employees)" diya gaya, aur woh Kafka, Cassandra, 20 microservices ke saath Kubernetes, aur multi-region active-active propose karta hai. Kya feedback doge?

Answer. Bataye scale ke liye over-engineering (5K users → kuch QPS). Ek service + Postgres + chhota cache + backups kaafi hai. Complexity cost aur failure modes badhaati hai. Pehle estimate karna chahiye tha aur design ko numbers ke hisaab se scale karna chahiye tha, saath mein batana ki usage badhe toh kaise evolve karenge.

Practice 3 — Deep dives chuno

"Concerts ke liye ticket-booking system (BookMyShow jaisa) design karo" mein kaunse 2–3 areas ka deep dive karoge aur kyun?

Answer. (1) Seat inventory & concurrency — double booking rokna (row locks / optimistic concurrency / expiry ke saath temporary holds). (2) Flash-sale traffic — bada concert khulte hi virtual waiting room / queue aur rate limiting. (3) Payment flow & idempotency — hold → pay → confirm, timeouts ke saath jo hold release kar dein.

docs.title: Revision checklist
docs.text:
• Interviewer kya evaluate karta hai aur top 5 red flags bata sakta hoon.
  • 45-min round ke liye 4 steps rough time budgets ke saath bol sakta hoon.
  • Features, scale, quality aur constraints ka mental question bank hai.
  • Design se pehle board pe requirements (FR / NFR / out of scope / estimates) likhta hoon.
  • Deep-dive topics kaise chunte hain aur seniority se kaise badalte hain, pata hai.
  • Bottlenecks, failures, monitoring aur agle 10× scale ke saath wrap up kar sakta hoon.

docs.title: Classic follow-ups — 10-second jawab
docs.text: Sawaal Jawab "Cache mar gaya toh?" Replicated cache; DB tak circuit breaker/rate limit; full traffic se pehle warm; degraded serve karo "Replica lag se stale data?" Us user ke liye thodi der leader se read-your-writes, ya replication position track karo "Hot key / celebrity?" Aage cache, hot key replicate, tod do, ya push ki jagah pull "Exactly-once?" End-to-end nahi; at-least-once + idempotency keys / dedup "Shard key kaise chunein?" High cardinality, main query se match, kam badle "SQL kyun nahi?" / "NoSQL kyun nahi?" Access pattern, chahiye transactions/joins, writes ka scale — naam lo "Eventually consistent store mein delete kaise?" Tombstones + compaction se pehle grace period "Ghadi peeche gayi (Snowflake)?" Detect karo; chhote drift pe wait; bade pe mana + alert "Ise monitor kaise karoge?" Latency, traffic, errors, saturation + system-specific lag metric (queue lag, fan-out lag, freshness)

docs.title: Aakhri 60-second self-check
docs.text:
• "Millions of users" waala architecture yaad se bana sakta hoon.
  • Kisi bhi prompt ke liye 3 minute mein QPS aur storage estimate kar sakta hoon.
  • Har case study ke APIs, data store, aur sabse mushkil hissa bata sakta hoon.
  • Jo bhi component jodta hoon, uski keemat bata sakta hoon.

Paper (saal) Kya sikhata hai Chapters Dynamo — Amazon (2007) Consistent hashing, quorums, vector clocks, sloppy quorum, Merkle trees 5, 6 Bigtable — Google (2006) Wide-column model, SSTables, memtables, tablets 6, 12 Cassandra — Facebook (2009) Dynamo-style distribution + Bigtable-style storage 6, 12 GFS — Google (2003) Chunked file storage, single master + replicas 15 MapReduce — Google (2004) Scale pe batch processing — autocomplete ka "aggregator" 13 Scaling Memcache at Facebook (2013) Cache invalidation, leases, regional caches 1, 11 TAO — Facebook (2013) Social-graph storage aur caching 11 Kafka — LinkedIn (2011) Log hi message queue 1, 10 Chubby (2006) / ZooKeeper (2010) Coordination, locks, service discovery 7, 12 Raft (2014) Samajh mein aane waala consensus aur leader election 1, 6 Spanner — Google (2012) Synchronised clocks ke saath globally consistent transactions 6, 7 Borg — Google (2015) Cluster scheduling — Kubernetes ka purvaj 14

docs.title: 2 · Agle level ke liye books
docs.text: Book Kyun Designing Data-Intensive Applications — Martin Kleppmann Replication, partitioning, transactions, consistency aur stream processing pe sabse achhi ek book. Is site ke baad padho. System Design Interview Volume 2 — Alex Xu & Sahn Lam Isi style mein 13 aur problems (neeche list dekho). Understanding Distributed Systems — Roberto Vitillo Interview designs aur production reality ke beech chhota, practical pul. Database Internals — Alex Petrov B-trees, LSM trees, replication aur consensus andar se. Site Reliability Engineering — Google Bade systems asal mein kaise chalte hain: SLOs, monitoring, incident response.

docs.title: 3 · Follow karne laayak engineering blogs
docs.text:
In companies ke engineering blogs search karo; architecture, migrations aur outages ke posts padho (post-mortems sabse zyada sikhate hain):

  • Global: Netflix, Uber, Meta, Google, Amazon (AWS Architecture), Discord, Cloudflare, Stripe, Shopify, Slack, Dropbox, Pinterest, Airbnb, LinkedIn, Figma.
  • India: Flipkart, Swiggy, Zomato, Razorpay, PhonePe, Zerodha, Hotstar/JioCinema (live-streaming scale ki kahaniyan), CRED.

Engineering blog post kaise padhein

Har post ke liye teen lines likho: problem (numbers ke saath), design choice, aur kya chhodna pada. Achhe interview answer ka shape exactly yahi hai.

docs.title: 4 · Practice ke liye aur problems
docs.text:
4-step framework aur 35-minute timer use karo. Hints jaan-bujh ke chhote hain — try karne ke baad hi kholo.

Proximity service (paas ke restaurants / Yelp)

Read-heavy; data lagbhag static. Locations ko geohash ya quadtree se index karo; popular areas cache karo; padosi cells bhi search karo.

Nearby friends (live locations)

WebSockets pe baar-baar location updates; har user ka pub/sub channel; sirf radius ke andar ke dosto ko fan out; stale locations pe TTL.

Google Maps

Map tiles pehle se render hoke CDN se serve; tiles mein bate graph pe routing; historical + live traffic se ETA.

Distributed message queue (Kafka jaisa)

Disk pe partitioned append-only logs; offsets ke saath consumer groups; leader/followers aur in-sync replicas ke saath replication.

Metrics monitoring & alerting

Time-series DB; push vs pull collection; downsampling aur retention tiers; streams pe evaluate hone waale alert rules.

Ad click aggregation

Windows ke saath stream processing (Flink); idempotent sinks se exactly-once jaisa; accuracy ke liye batch se reconcile.

Hotel / ticket reservation

Inventory pe strong consistency; double booking roko (row locks / optimistic concurrency); idempotent payments; expire hone waale holds.

Distributed email service

SMTP ingestion, spam filtering, har user ka mailbox storage, search index, attachments object storage mein.

S3 jaisa object storage

Metadata service ko data nodes se alag; erasure coding vs replication; multipart upload; versioning.

Real-time gaming leaderboard

Har leaderboard ka Redis sorted set; game/region se shard; durable storage pe samay-samay pe snapshots.

Payment system & digital wallet

Double-entry ledger; har jagah idempotency keys; payment provider se reconciliation; state machines se exactly-once effects.

Stock exchange

Determinism ke liye har symbol ka single-threaded matching engine; sequencer; bahut kam latency; event log se replay.

Collaborative document editing (Google Docs)

Operational transformation ya CRDTs; har document ka session server; presence cursors; snapshots + operation log.

Ride-hailing (driver matching)

Driver locations geo index mein (Redis mein geohash cells); har shehar ki matching service; har cell ke supply/demand se surge pricing.

docs.title: 5 · 30-din ka practice plan
docs.text: Din Yeh karo 1–3 Chapter 1 ka architecture yaad se dobara banao; Chapter 2 ke saare practice problems bina dekhe dobara karo. 4–7 Building blocks: token bucket, consistent hash ring aur Snowflake Java mein scratch se implement karo. 8–15 Roz ek case study, timed, zor se. Chapter se compare karo; jo chhoota woh likho. 16–25 Upar ki list se roz ek naya problem. Khud ko record karo; khamoshi aur hawa-hawai baatein sun ke pakdo. 26–28 Dost ke saath do mock interviews (roles badlo — interview lena utna hi sikhata hai jitna dena). 29–30 Cheat Sheet padho; apne do sabse kamzor problems dobara karo.

docs.title: 6 · High-level design se aage
docs.text:
• Low-level design (LLD) / object-oriented design — class diagrams, design patterns (strategy, observer, factory…), SOLID, concurrency. Kai interviews mein LLD round hota hai (parking lot, elevator, rate limiter class design).
  • Hands-on — Docker se Redis, Kafka aur Postgres locally chalao; cache aur load test ke saath ek chhota URL shortener banao; dekho kya tootta hai.
  • Jo banao use chalao — apni kisi cheez pe monitoring (Prometheus + Grafana) set up karo aur uske graphs padhna practice karo.

docs.title: Aakhri baat
docs.text:
Yahan ka har chapter kuch hi sawaalon pe aakar ruka: access pattern kya hai, numbers kya hain, sabse pehle kya tootega, aur hum kya chhodne ko taiyaar hain? Agar tum yeh sawaal shaanti se pooch sakte ho aur jawabon tak zor se reason kar sakte ho, toh tum interview ke liye taiyaar ho — aur usse bhi zyada zaroori, kaam ke liye.
